item.title: Artturi Lehkonen, Avalanche take aim at Predators
item.description: Following their "most complete effort of the year," the Colorado Avalanche will look to make it back-to-back victories when they travel to Nashville to face the Predators on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Following their "most complete effort of the year," the Colorado Avalanche will look to make it back-to-back victories when they travel to Nashville to face the Predators on Sunday. Nathan MacKinnon collected a goal and three assists in the Avalanche's 6-3 victory over the visiting Tampa Bay Lightning on Friday night. Martin Necas added a goal and two assists, while Artturi Lehkonen and defenseman Devon Toews had one of each. Nazem Kadri and Fedor Svechkov also tallied for Colorado, which snapped a two-game skid. Mackenzie Blackwood made 31 saves for his fourth win of the season. "That was probably our most complete effort of the year," Avalanche coach Jared Bednar said. "Close as you can get with all the penalties in the second period. I thought we had a great first, 5-on-5 in the second was really good. I mean, you're killing, like I think we had six straight penalties right, when it all adds up at one point in the game. "So you're only using half your bench. The challenge was going to be having those guys stay in it, but then they had a good third period, too." Lehkonen, who paces the Avalanche with nine goals, is riding a six-game point streak (six goals, three assists). "He's very underrated. He's always in a good spot," Necas said of Lehkonen. "He creates so much space out there for me and (MacKinnon) to play a little bit around. Feels like every time he gets the puck, it's a chance. He's a great player. He plays great defense. You don't really find players like him." MacKinnon has a team-high 13 assists and 20 points in 11 games. Blackwood, Sunday's expected starter, is 4-3-0 with a 2.90 goals-against average and an .889 save percentage. In eight career games against the Predators, Blackwood is 2-4-1 with a 3.60 GAA and an .893 save percentage. Sunday is the first of four meetings between the Central Division rivals. They each won two games against the other in 2025-26. Nashville returns home looking to avoid a third straight loss after dropping a 3-2 overtime decision in Pittsburgh on Saturday night. "We're going to have to learn to take care of the puck better," Predators coach Andrew Brunette said. "We lost momentum by not taking care of the puck." Steven Stamkos and Jayden Struble each scored for the Predators, who have lost five of their last six games (1-2-3). Juuse Saros made 34 saves on Saturday but dropped to 3-2-3. "We played north, and we played fast. I thought in the second period we kind of lost that a little bit," defenseman Brady Skjei said. "Held on a little bit in the third. If we don't have (Saros), that's a different story. He played unbelievable." Stamkos has a team-high five goals and 11 points through 10 games. Justus Annunen, expected to start Sunday, made 25 saves in the Preds' 6-0 loss to the Boston Bruins on Thursday, his season debut. --Field Level Media

item.title: CON O Cómo los ataques de Ucrania a instalaciones energéticas rusas agravaron la ruptura con Trump
item.description: Las relaciones entre el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, y su par ucraniano, Volodimir Zelenski, han sufrido un fuerte deterioro en las últimas semanas, con críticas abiertas entre ambos.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: Las relaciones entre el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, y su par ucraniano, Volodimir Zelenski, han sufrido un fuerte deterioro en las últimas semanas, con críticas abiertas entre ambos. Los líderes mantienen desde hace tiempo una relación tensa, pero la frustración de Trump por los ataques ucranianos contra la infraestructura energética rusa ha desencadenado una crisis que, según temen los partidarios de Kiev, podría poner en peligro el apoyo de Washington en el futuro. Así es como se deterioró la relación: ¿CUÁL ES LA HISTORIA DE LAS TENSIONES TRUMP-ZELENSKI? Trump se ha mostrado escéptico respecto a la implicación de Estados Unidos en Ucrania desde su primer mandato, cuando, poco después de asumir el cargo a principios de 2017, se le pidió que proporcionara ayuda a Ucrania y aprobó la venta de misiles Javelin a Kiev. "Todos los que le rodeaban querían que lo hiciera, lo presionaron mucho y, al final, autorizó la venta de los Javelin, muy a regañadientes", afirmó un exfuncionario que habló bajo condición de anonimato. "No lo consideraba un interés fundamental de EEUU. Era un asunto europeo". El primer encuentro importante de Trump con Zelenski tuvo lugar en una llamada telefónica de julio de 2019, en la que el republicano pidió al líder ucraniano que investigara a su rival demócrata, Joe Biden, y a su hijo Hunter, a cambio del apoyo militar que el Congreso había autorizado. Ese episodio condujo al primer proceso de juicio político de Trump. Biden venció a Trump en las elecciones presidenciales de 2020. Trump también ha fomentado una relación con el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, que va en contra de las normas de la política exterior de Washington, pero que se hace eco de sus cálidos vínculos con líderes autoritarios como Xi Jinping, de China, y el líder de Corea del Norte, Kim Jong-un. "Trump siempre ha querido mejorar las relaciones con Rusia", afirmó el exfuncionario. ¿QUÉ PROFUNDIZÓ LA BRECHA ENTRE LOS LÍDERES? La frustración actual de Trump se centra en los ataques de Kiev contra la infraestructura del diésel rusa. Los precios del gasóleo han alcanzado máximos históricos desde que EEUU e Israel iniciaron una guerra contra Irán en febrero, y los costos energéticos mundiales se dispararon. Los legisladores del Partido Republicano de Trump se enfrentan a la ira de los votantes por la inflación de cara a las elecciones de mitad de legislatura del 3 de noviembre. El 13 de septiembre, Trump comenzó a pedir públicamente a Ucrania que dejara de atacar la infraestructura del gasóleo. La semana siguiente, el secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, afirmó que a Washington también le preocupaba que Ucrania hubiera atacado envíos de petróleo vinculados a EEUU. Ucrania se ha negado a detener los ataques, alegando que su campaña con drones de largo alcance es su única respuesta viable a casi cinco años de bombardeos rusos. Moscú se vio obligada en julio a prohibir las exportaciones de gasóleo como parte de una serie de medidas para hacer frente a la escasez de combustible en el país. Indignado por la rebeldía de Zelenski, Trump anunció el 9 de octubre un acuerdo para comprar gasóleo a Moscú, emitiendo una licencia general temporal que permite que el gasóleo ruso llegue al mercado mundial. También suspendió las sanciones contra Rusia autorizadas por un proyecto de ley que él mismo promulgó en septiembre. Suriya Jayanti, una exfuncionaria estadounidense que dirige una empresa del sector energético en Ucrania, afirmó que los ataques rusos contra la red eléctrica ucraniana han aumentado, a pesar de que Trump anunciara unilateralmente un alto el fuego energético el 11 de octubre. "Para todos en Kiev está claro que el objetivo no es realmente un alto el fuego energético, sino que se trata, en realidad, de un intento de paralizar a Ucrania y proporcionar a Rusia una ventaja decisiva", afirmó Jayanti, quien también es investigadora principal del think tank Atlantic Council. ¿HA AMENAZADO EEUU CON RETIRAR APOYO A UCRANIA? Zelenski ha dicho que los responsables militares ucranianos habían sido amenazados por sus homólogos estadounidenses, quienes les advirtieron que, si continuaban los ataques contra la infraestructura energética, Washington dejaría de compartir información de inteligencia. Un funcionario estadounidense familiarizado con la situación desmintió la versión de Kiev. Hablando bajo condición de anonimato, el funcionario estadounidense afirmó que no se ha producido ningún aumento de la presión sobre Ucrania. "No tenemos que presionar a Zelenski. Si quiere llegar a un acuerdo, lo hará. Creo que Putin está ejerciendo una presión enorme y que él (Zelenski) está ejerciendo cierta presión sobre Rusia, pero a Rusia no parece importarle demasiado". Trump afirmó el jueves que había pedido al CEO de SpaceX, Elon Musk, que restableciera el acceso de Ucrania a su sistema de satélites Starlink. La interrupción del servicio de Starlink obstaculizó temporalmente las operaciones militares con drones de Kiev y avivó el temor a Ucrania quedara indefensa ante los ataques de Rusia de cara al invierno boreal. ¿DÓNDE SE ENCUENTRAN LAS NEGOCIACIONES DE PAZ MOSCÚ-KIEV? Los esfuerzos de paz han continuado, pero hasta ahora no han dado resultados tangibles. En las conversaciones celebradas en Oslo el 20 de octubre, Ucrania presentó nuevas propuestas, y el yerno y enviado de Trump, Jared Kushner, reiteró la exigencia del republicano de que Ucrania dejara de atacar las refinerías de gasóleo rusas. Al día siguiente, el enviado especial Steven Witkoff se reunió con Putin en San Petersburgo. Putin accedió a liberar al ciudadano estadounidense Stephen Hubbard, en lo que ambos países calificaron de gesto de buena voluntad. Zelenski afirmó el viernes que los negociadores de Ucrania, Rusia y EEUU se reunirían en Abu Dabi durante la primera quincena de noviembre, lo que podría ser un preludio de una reunión entre los líderes de los tres países. Las últimas conversaciones de paz mediadas por Washington tuvieron lugar en febrero.

item.title: Unbeaten 76ers, Pistons test mettle in early-season showdown
item.description: The Philadelphia 76ers and Detroit Pistons are expected to be contenders in the Eastern Conference this season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Philadelphia 76ers and Detroit Pistons are expected to be contenders in the Eastern Conference this season. The two teams have lived up to expectations so far, creating an intriguing early-season matchup between unbeaten foes Sunday in Philadelphia. The 76ers are 3-0 with their new star-studded lineup, which debuted with a road win over the defending champion New York Knicks and followed that up with a 29-point comeback victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers. Most recently, Philadelphia topped the Milwaukee Bucks 127-116 on Saturday behind Joel Embiid's 10th career triple-double. The former MVP registered 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists, while Jaylen Brown added 27 points and Tyrese Maxey chipped in with 26. "We can't be satisfied being 3-0," Brown said. "We can't be satisfied with where we're at right now. We're building for something, so we've got to get better." One area in which the Sixers can improve is getting off to better starts. They scuffled through the first quarter against the Knicks and then trailed the Cavaliers by 24 points at halftime. Even against the winless Bucks, Philadelphia held a one-point lead in the waning seconds of the first half before Maxey banked in a half-court shot at the buzzer. "As we're going here, it's still really early for us. ... We're trying to learn things that we're going to polish quick," coach Nick Nurse said. LeBron James (back/sciatica) sat out Saturday's victory, while Embiid is expected to rest Sunday. That could mean a bigger offensive role for VJ Edgecombe, who scored a season-high 17 points Saturday, and sixth man Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, who made four 3-pointers against Milwaukee. "I'm just excited and having fun right now, man," Caldwell-Pope said. "This is a good group. We're still putting it together, but it's looking good." Things are looking good for the Pistons, as well. After finishing with the best record in the East last season, Detroit is 2-0 in the early going with quality wins over the Boston Celtics and Miami Heat. In Friday's 128-111 win in Miami, John Collins scored 23 points to pace six double-digit scorers. Paul Reed added 19 points and 11 rebounds in a reserve role, while Duncan Robinson knocked down five 3-pointers and finished with 17 points. "That's where we can create trouble, right?" coach J.B. Bickerstaff said of the Pistons' depth. "We have so many people that can be used as weapons that we can just take what the defense gives us. We don't have to try to overmanipulate things." Detroit's depth proved critical because Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren were held to four points apiece before leaving with injuries. Thompson (ankle) is questionable to face Philadelphia, while Duren (hamstring) will miss Sunday's contest. Despite losing two of their top defensive players, the Pistons held the Heat to 38.2% shooting from the field and 29.4% from 3-point range. Still, Bickerstaff was far from satisfied. "We know we're still finding our way defensively," he said. "I don't think we've been our best that way yet." The Pistons won all four matchups with the Sixers in 2025-26, recording 22- and 23-point victories in the final two meetings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Papa León pide que cese violencia en Yemen dos semanas después de someterse a intervención quirúrgica
item.description: El papa León pidió el domingo el fin de la violencia en Yemen, en su discurso a los fieles desde la ventana que da a la plaza de San Pedro, menos de dos semanas después de haberse sometido a una intervención quirúrgica por un cáncer de pulmón.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El papa León pidió el domingo el fin de la violencia en Yemen, en su discurso a los fieles desde la ventana que da a la plaza de San Pedro, menos de dos semanas después de haberse sometido a una intervención quirúrgica por un cáncer de pulmón. El pontífice, de 71 años, afirmó estar especialmente preocupado por la situación humanitaria en la ciudad yemení de Taiz, "donde la población sufre por la falta de alimentos, agua y asistencia médica". Saludó con la mano y sonrió a la multitud tras llegar a la ventana sin ayuda, el mismo lugar desde donde anunció el 11 de octubre que se sometería a una operación para extirpar un pequeño tumor en un pulmón, en lo que supuso el primer susto relacionado con su salud desde el inicio de su papado. "Hago un llamamiento sincero para que cesen las hostilidades, de modo que la población de Yemen y de toda la región pueda vivir en paz", afirmó León con voz firme y clara. El papa dijo que también rezaba por los fallecidos y heridos en el "ataque terrorista contra fieles ortodoxos" perpetrado el viernes en la iglesia de Hamoud, en Jordania. "Me siento cercano a esa comunidad y a todo el país, conocido por la convivencia pacífica y respetuosa de las diferentes religiones". León instó a todos a acompañar con sus oraciones un encuentro de líderes religiosos para promover la paz que tendrá lugar el martes en la ciudad italiana de Asís, al que tenía previsto asistir pero canceló su visita por recomendación de los médicos para facilitar su recuperación. El papa fue sometido a una intervención quirúrgica el 13 de octubre en la que se le extirpó el lóbulo inferior del pulmón derecho tras serle diagnosticado un adenocarcinoma, el tipo más común de cáncer de pulmón. La semana pasada, los médicos afirmaron que no necesitaría más tratamiento, lo que indica que el tumor no se había extendido.

item.title: Lucas Pinheiro Braathen vence prova de abertura do slalom gigante masculino na Áustria
item.description: O campeão olímpico brasileiro Lucas Pinheiro Braathen deu sequência à sua excelente fase ao vencer neste domingo a prova de abertura do slalom gigante masculino da temporada de esqui alpino, na Áustria.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O campeão olímpico brasileiro Lucas Pinheiro Braathen deu sequência à sua excelente fase ao vencer neste domingo a prova de abertura do slalom gigante masculino da temporada de esqui alpino, na Áustria. Nascido na Noruega, Pinheiro Braathen, que conquistou o ouro nos Jogos Olímpicos de Milão-Cortina em fevereiro e venceu as duas últimas provas de slalom gigante da temporada 2025-26, foi 0,24 segundo mais rápido do que os demais na primeira descida pela pista da geleira Rettenbach, em Soelden. A prova teve seu percurso encurtado devido aos fortes ventos. Ele confirmou a vitória com vantagem de 0,48 segundo sobre o suíço Loic Meillard, medalhista de ouro olímpico no slalom. O pentacampeão geral da Copa do Mundo, Marco Odermatt, terminou em terceiro lugar, apenas 0,01 segundo atrás de seu compatriota, após registrar o melhor tempo na segunda descida. "Que alívio poder abrir a temporada dessa forma", disse Pinheiro Braathen, que continua invicto no slalom gigante desde sua conquista olímpica. "Trabalhei muito durante todo o verão. Estive buscando novas motivações, novos caminhos para evoluir a partir do ouro olímpico do ano passado e do Globo de Cristal do slalom gigante. E estamos mirando novas metas, novos objetivos." O norte-americano River Radamus terminou em quarto lugar depois de ter sido apenas o 15º colocado na primeira descida. Já o britânico Freddy Carrick-Smith, que largou com o número 46, subiu para a 21ª posição após a primeira descida e terminou a prova em 12º. Alguns nomes de destaque abandonaram a competição, entre eles o italiano Giovanni Franzoni e o norueguês Atle Lie McGrath. No sábado, a norte-americana Paula Moltzan venceu a prova feminina de abertura do slalom gigante. A temporada masculina da Copa do Mundo prossegue com uma prova de slalom em Levi, na Finlândia, em 15 de novembro, um dia depois da disputa feminina no mesmo local. Pinheiro Braathen venceu o slalom de Levi na temporada passada, sua primeira vitória competindo sob a bandeira do Brasil. (Reportagem de Alan Baldwin)

item.title: Brazil's Pinheiro Braathen wins season-opening men's giant slalom
item.description: Brazil's Olympic champion Lucas Pinheiro Braathen continued where he left off by winning the opening men's giant slalom of the Alpine ski season in Austria on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazil's Olympic champion [USN:L6N4681C1 TEXT:"Lucas Pinheiro Braathen continued"] where he left off by winning the opening men's giant slalom of the Alpine ski season in Austria on Sunday. The Norwegian-born skier, who [USN:L8N3ZA08E TEXT:"took gold at the Milano Cortina Games"] in February and [USN:L6N40C0XP TEXT:"won the last two giants"] of the 2025-26 season, was 0.24 of a second faster than the rest on a first run down Soelden's Rettenbach glacier piste that was shortened due to strong winds. He went on to win by 0.48 from Switzerland's Loic Meillard, the Olympic slalom gold medallist. Five-time defending overall World Cup champion Marco Odermatt was third, 0.01 slower than his compatriot, after going fastest on the second run. "What a relief to be able to open the show in this way," said Pinheiro Braathen, who is unbeaten in giant since his Olympic success. "I have worked so hard this whole summer. "I've been searching for new curiosities, new paths to evolve from last year's Olympic gold and the (giant slalom crystal) globe. And you know, we're headed towards new goals, new objectives." American River Radamus finished fourth from 15th after the first run and Britain's Freddy Carrick-Smith went from bib number 46 to 21st and then 12th at the finish while some big names fell, including Italy's Giovanni Franzoni and Norway's Atle Lie McGrath. American Paula Moltzan won the [USN:L6N46A02Y TEXT:"opening women's giant slalom"] on Saturday. The men's World Cup season continues with a slalom in Levi, Finland, on November 15, a day after the women compete there. Pinheiro Braathen [USN:L1N3WS02D TEXT:"won last season's Levi slalom"], his first victory with the Brazilian flag.

item.title: Lula vota em São Bernardo e agradece por mobilização popular na campanha
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) votou na manhã deste domingo em São Bernardo do Campo, São Paulo, e disse ser grato pela mobilização popular vista nas ruas ao redor do país nas últimas semanas, ressaltando que acha que o Brasil “não vai eleger um mentiroso”, em referência ao senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) votou na manhã deste domingo em São Bernardo do Campo, São Paulo, e disse ser grato pela mobilização popular vista nas ruas ao redor do país nas últimas semanas, ressaltando que acha que o Brasil “não vai eleger um mentiroso”, em referência ao senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). “O que o povo fez comigo nesses dias é uma coisa que não tem como pagar, é muita generosidade, é muito carinho, é muito amor e eu serei eternamente grato ao comportamento do povo”, disse o petista em entrevista a jornalistas. O presidente, que tenta a reeleição a um quarto mandato não consecutivo, votou em uma escola em São Bernardo do Campo, berço político do Partido dos Trabalhadores. Ele foi acompanhado pela primeira-dama Janja Lula da Silva, o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin e os ex-ministros Fernando Haddad, Marina Silva e Simone Tebet. “Temos que fazer uma opção se a gente quer um Brasil que distribua milhões de livros didáticos nas escolas ou se a gente quer um Brasil que distribua a possibilidade de comprar um milhão de armas”, afirmou, acrescentando que seu oponente trabalha para atender interesses dos Estados Unidos. Na entrevista, Lula disse estar disputando as eleições “com um cidadão chamado mentira” e acrescentou que Flávio “não é capaz de dizer uma verdade em momento algum”. Ele ainda defendeu que o resultado das eleições seja respeitado e repudiou casos de violência política registrados no país nos últimos dias.

item.title: Grupos de protesto e sindicatos na França convocam novas manifestações
item.description: Grupos de protesto e sindicatos da França convocaram neste domingo novas manifestações, enquanto buscam manter a pressão sobre o governo após uma ampla operação de segurança ajudar a conter os distúrbios durante protestos realizados em todo o país no sábado.
item.dc:creator: Crispian Balmer, Juliette Jabkhiro
item.content:encoded: Grupos de protesto e sindicatos da França convocaram neste domingo novas manifestações, enquanto buscam manter a pressão sobre o governo após uma ampla operação de segurança ajudar a conter os distúrbios durante protestos realizados em todo o país no sábado. O Ministério do Interior informou que 410 mil pessoas participaram das marchas de sábado. As autoridades mobilizaram 70 mil policiais, o que ajudou a evitar a repetição dos saques e atos de vandalismo que atingiram diversas cidades em 17 de outubro. Líderes sindicais convocaram novos protestos para o próximo sábado e uma greve nacional em 5 de novembro, afirmando que a insatisfação com salários, custo de vida e serviços públicos está se espalhando muito além do movimento estudantil que iniciou as mobilizações no mês passado. "Estamos vendo uma agregação de revoltas", disse Murielle Guilbert, copresidente da central sindical de esquerda Solidaires, à emissora BFM TV. Segundo ela, reivindicações de estudantes, trabalhadores, bombeiros e outros grupos estão convergindo. "Conclamamos as pessoas a ocuparem as ruas no próximo sábado." O sindicato de professores SUD Education afirmou que participará da manifestação de 31 de outubro, enquanto a grande central sindical CGT informou que tomará uma decisão ao longo da semana. POUCO ESPAÇO PARA MACRON RESPONDER Os Coletes Amarelos, movimento de base que surgiu em 2018 em oposição aos impostos sobre combustíveis, também convocaram mobilizações em massa para o próximo sábado, incluindo atos diante de prefeituras e da Assembleia Nacional. "Há indignação neste país. Ela está crescendo nas escolas e universidades, nas rotatórias, nos bairros, nas fazendas e nos locais de trabalho", afirmou a ativista Azelma Sigaux a jornalistas. Em 2019, o presidente Emmanuel Macron conseguiu encontrar recursos para reduzir os custos dos combustíveis em resposta às reivindicações dos Coletes Amarelos. Sete anos depois, as contas públicas pressionadas deixam pouco espaço para que ele atenda às demandas dos manifestantes. Além disso, seu mandato termina em abril do próximo ano, e seu partido de centro não possui mais a maioria necessária para aprovar legislação de grande alcance. O governo iniciou negociações com sindicatos e representantes estudantis na tentativa de conter a crise, mas líderes dos protestos afirmam que as medidas propostas até agora são insuficientes. "Não recebemos nenhuma resposta deste governo", disse Guilbert. Sindicatos policiais afirmaram neste domingo que não dispõem de efetivo suficiente para sustentar por muito tempo o elevado nível de mobilização que, no sábado, ajudou a limitar os distúrbios a confrontos esporádicos em várias cidades, incluindo Paris e Marselha. Segundo o Ministério do Interior, 1.314 pessoas foram presas no sábado, metade do número registrado na semana anterior. Cerca de 50 policiais ficaram feridos, ante mais de 1.000 na semana passada. REPERCUSSÃO ALÉM DA FRANÇA Os protestos tiveram repercussão para além das fronteiras francesas. No sábado, a polícia belga utilizou gás lacrimogêneo e spray de pimenta durante confrontos com manifestantes antigoverno em Bruxelas. Na Albânia, protestos pacíficos iniciados no fim de maio se transformaram neste mês em confrontos violentos e ações também foram registradas em várias cidades italianas pela segunda semana consecutiva. (Reportagem de Crispian Balmer e Juliette Jabkhiro)

item.title: Pope Leo calls for Yemen violence to end, in address two weeks after surgery
item.description: Pope Leo called for an end to the violence in Yemen on Sunday, as he addressed the faithful from the window over St Peter's Square less than two weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pope Leo called for an end to the violence in Yemen on Sunday, as he addressed the faithful from the window over St Peter's Square less than two weeks after having surgery for lung cancer. The 71-year-old pontiff said he was particularly concerned about the humanitarian situation in the southwestern [USN:L6N4670EA TEXT:"Yemeni city of Taiz"], "where the population suffers due to the lack of food, water and medical assistance". He waved and smiled to the crowds after reaching the window unaided — the same spot where [USN:L1N45X029 TEXT:"he announced"] on October 11 that he would have an operation to remove a small growth on his lung, in the first health scare of his papacy. "I'm making a heartfelt appeal for the hostilities to stop, so that the people in Yemen and across the entire region can live in peace," he said in a very firm and clear voice. The pope said he was also praying for those who had been killed and wounded in the "terrorist attack [USN:L1N4690IY TEXT:"against Orthodox faithful" at the Hamoud church"] in Jordan on Friday. "I'm close to that community and the entire country, which is known for the peaceful and respectful coexistence of different religions," the pontiff said. Pope Leo urged everyone to accompany with prayers a meeting of religious leaders to promote peace that will take place in the Italian city of Assisi on Tuesday. He had been due to attend that event, but [USN:L8N4690JP TEXT:"cancelled his visit"] on the advice of doctors to aid his recovery, the Vatican said on Friday. The pope had the lower lobe of his right lung removed in surgery [USN:L1N45Z08S TEXT:"on October 13"] after being diagnosed with [USN:L8N46006S TEXT:"adenocarcinoma"], the most common form of lung cancer. Last week, doctors said he would [USN:L1N46710S TEXT:"not need any further therapy"], indicating that his tumour had not spread.

item.title: Paris game set to kick off in calm atmosphere after fresh demonstrations
item.description: Protests largely overshadowed the build-up to the first NFL regular-season game.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Daheron
item.content:encoded: The Pittsburgh Steelers and the New Orleans Saints were set to kick off the first NFL regular-season game in Paris at 2.30 p.m. (1330 GMT) on Sunday, in a calm and festive atmosphere, a day after fresh demonstrations drew more than 100,000 people into the French capital. The nationwide protests largely overshadowed the build-up to the game, with some fan and NFL [USN:L6N46912R TEXT:"events cancelled"] over the weekend, mainly due to their location in central Paris. On Sunday, as Saturday’s rain gave way to sunshine, the mood was peaceful around the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, some 10km (6 miles) north of Paris centre and more than 13km (8 miles) from Porte d'Italie, where Saturday's protests began in southern Paris. James Brown, a 51-year-old Saints fan who travelled to Paris especially for the game, told Reuters the atmosphere around the stadium was "wonderful, really good". The police presence appeared neither heavy nor unusual at the Stade de France, which hosted rugby sevens and athletics during the 2024 Paris Olympics and regularly serves as the home ground for the French national rugby and soccer teams. Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators marched in France on Saturday, with largely peaceful rallies giving way to clashes in Paris and Marseille as night fell despite a huge security operation aimed at preventing a repeat of last week's unrest. The main demonstration took place on the southeastern fringes of Paris, where at least 110,000 people turned out to denounce rising living costs and growing inequality. "We didn't notice much yesterday," 38-year-old Steelers fan Lukas Baldridge told Reuters. "We came in, went to a bar, got some drinks, got dinner, went home, didn't see any protesting." "Streets were closed. Most shops were closed. That felt unusual maybe but I don't know enough about Paris to know what is normal and what's not normal."

item.title: What are Brazilian voters' main concerns?
item.description: Brazilians headed to the ballot box on Sunday, in a runoff vote that pits right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, against leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Isabel Teles
item.content:encoded: Brazilians headed to the ballot box on Sunday, in a runoff vote that pits right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, against leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Here are the main themes that have driven the campaign: INFLATION Cost-of-living concerns are widespread. More than two-thirds of respondents told a Quaest poll in August their purchasing power [USN:L6N459162 TEXT:"had declined"] versus the previous year. Annual inflation stood at 4.58% in the 12 months through September, above the central bank's 3% target, pushing prices — including for food — higher Lula has pledged to implement measures to allow for steady cuts in borrowing costs and keep inflation under control Bolsonaro wants to reduce and stabilize public debt to bring interest rates closer to international levels and steer inflation toward the central bank's target CRIME Crime is another major [USN:L1N45Z0NR TEXT:"concern"] for Brazilians. While Brazil's homicide rate fell by 40% over the last decade, improvements in fighting crime have been uneven, according to the Brazilian Public Security Forum, a think tank. Bolsonaro has pledged a heavy-handed approach to criminals, promising maximum-security prisons and chemical castration for serious sexual offenses Lula wants to increase the federal prison system's capacity to hold gang leaders, while still investing in poor areas to reduce the influence of organized crime CORRUPTION Corruption is also at the top of voters' minds, with both Lula's circle and Bolsonaro [USN:L6N46611M TEXT:"facing scrutiny"] in high-profile cases. A major scandal that led to the collapse of mid-size lender Banco Master has sparked multiple probes, including into [USN:L6N3ZZ1EP TEXT:"Bolsonaro"] over alleged corruption and money laundering, accusations he denies Bolsonaro has pledged to fight corruption by shielding state-run companies and pension funds from political appointments and expanding transparency in public spending Lula has vowed to deepen anti-corruption and transparency policies even as his son - who has denied the allegations - is being investigated in probes involving alleged influence peddling, corruption and fraud PUBLIC FINANCES Brazil's public finances are under pressure, especially due to pensions and social benefits. The difficult fiscal outlook has sparked fears of welfare cuts, while many Brazilians are struggling with debt arrears due to years of double-digit interest rates. Public debt has risen by more than 10 percentage points during Lula's current term, reaching [USN:L1N45M0ES TEXT:"82.9%"] of gross domestic product Brazil's benchmark interest rate of [USN:L6N458186 TEXT:"13.75%"] remains among the highest in the world Long-term interest rates [USN:L1N45R06Y TEXT:"fell sharply"] after Bolsonaro's stronger-than-expected first-round performance He has promised to ramp up [USN:L1N4580UE TEXT:"fiscal adjustment"], targeting 1.5% of GDP improvement in the primary balance within 18 months to lower borrowing costs Lula has reiterated commitments to improve Brazil's primary balance targeting an [USN:L1N44S10B TEXT:"effective surplus"] near 1.3% of GDP by 2030, versus a projected 0.4% deficit this year FOREIGN POLICY After US President Donald Trump imposed [USN:L6N3TR0ZD TEXT:"tariffs"] on a swathe of Brazilian goods in 2025, foreign policy became a more prominent issue for many Brazilians. Bolsonaro has courted Trump and other right-wing allies globally He wants to rebuild ties with Argentina, the US and Israel, arguing relations with each are close to breaking point Lula has campaigned for a foreign policy based on multilateralism and stronger ties with the Mercosur bloc of South American states and the BRICS nations ($1 = 5.0086 reais)

item.title: L'Arabie saoudite intercepte des missiles et des drones
item.description: L'Arabie saoudite a intercepté dimanche des drones et des missiles au-dessus de sa capitale Ryad et du sud de son territoire, a dit la coalition emmenée par les Saoudiens contre les Houthis au Yémen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Arabie saoudite a intercepté dimanche des drones et des missiles au-dessus de sa capitale Ryad et du sud de son territoire, a dit la coalition emmenée par les Saoudiens contre les Houthis au Yémen. La défense civile saoudienne a émis des alertes pour Ryad, Abha et Khamis Mushait, dans le sud du pays, avant de les lever au bout de quelques minutes. Deux drones et un missile balistique ont été tirés en direction de Ryad et un missile de croisière l'a été contre Khamis Mushait, a dit la coalition saoudienne au Yémen. Elle a par la suite déclaré avoir intercepté 10 missiles tirés en direction du sud de l'Arabie saoudite. Les Houthis, soutenus par l'Iran, ont menacé de prendre à nouveau pour cible l'aéroport international de Ryad, dont deux terminaux ont rouvert dimanche après une double attaque meurtrière début octobre. Ils ont affirmé avoir attaqué samedi l'aéroport et des installations pétrolières saoudiennes. L'Arabie n'a pas réagi directement à ces affirmations.

item.title: Ouchakov, conseiller de Poutine, prône une implication européenne dans les efforts de paix en Ukraine
item.description: L'Europe doit être impliquée dans les discussions sur une issue au conflit entre l'Ukraine et la Russie car sa position pourrait être déterminante, a déclaré dimanche Iouri Ouchakov, conseiller diplomatique du président russe Vladimir Poutine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Europe doit être impliquée dans les discussions sur une issue au conflit entre l'Ukraine et la Russie car sa position pourrait être déterminante, a déclaré dimanche Iouri Ouchakov, conseiller diplomatique du président russe Vladimir Poutine. Une implication européenne est notamment rendue nécessaire par le fait que les Etats-Unis ne sont pas parvenus à exercer suffisamment de pression sur l'Ukraine pour que cette dernière accepte un accord de paix, a ajouté Iouri Ouchakov dans une interview avec le journaliste de la télévision publique russe Pavel Zaroubine. "Avant, il semblait qu'après Anchorage, l'administration américaine pourrait être en mesure d'imposer quelque chose et de contraindre Kyiv à s'y soumettre. Mais à ce stade, cela n'a pas vraiment fonctionné", a déclaré Iouri Ouchakov, en référence à la rencontre en 2025 en Alaska entre les présidents américain Donald Trump et russe Vladimir Poutine. "C'est parce qu'il ne suffit pas de parler uniquement avec Kyiv, nous devons parler avec l'Europe tout entière, qui soutient totalement Kyiv", a-t-il ajouté. Iouri Ouchakov a déclaré que la Russie était prête à reprendre des pourparlers à trois avec l'Ukraine et les Etats-Unis après le Jour de l'unité nationale célébré le 4 novembre en Russie. Le Kremlin a déjà déclaré mercredi que Vladimir Poutine était disposé à relancer dès novembre des pourparlers avec l'Ukraine sous l'égide des Etats-Unis. Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré vendredi que des négociateurs ukrainiens, russes et américains étaient convenus de participer à une réunion technique dans la première quinzaine du mois de novembre à Abou Dhabi, en formulant l'espoir qu'un sommet entre les dirigeants des trois pays suivrait. Iouri Ouchakov a fait état de préparatifs d'un sommet entre Vladimir Poutine, Donald Trump et le président chinois Xi Jinping. Une telle rencontre pourrait avoir lieu en marge du sommet du forum de Coopération économique pour l'Asie-Pacifique(Apec) prévu en Chine les 18 et 19 novembre.

item.title: Carrick drops United captain Fernandes to bench against Bournemouth
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has dropped captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench for Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but said the decision was based solely on football considerations.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has dropped captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench for Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but said the decision was based solely on football considerations. Fernandes questioned United's approach after Wednesday's 4-1 Champions League thrashing at Como, suggesting the side had allowed their opponents too much time and space by sitting back rather than pressing aggressively. Asked before kickoff whether Fernandes had been left out for football reasons or other factors, Carrick told Sky Sports: "Pure football." "When you have options it's always a difficult decision. We have to make the right one for today and the team to get that performance we want," he added. Defender Harry Maguire will wear the captain's armband instead. After Wednesday's shambolic loss, Fernandes told TNT Sports: "The coaching staff decided not to press man-to-man, but instead to sit back and look to win the ball; the problem, however, is that you give teams like that confidence when you allow them that space." The Portugal international added that teams under pressure sometimes needed to be "braver" and take risks by pressing higher up the pitch. Carrick had refused to rule out disciplinary action when asked about the comments at his pre-match press conference on Friday. The midfielder was named among the substitutes against Bournemouth. Since Carrick's first game in charge in January, Fernandes has registered more assists (14) and created more chances (96) than any player in Europe's big five leagues. United began the day 15th in the table with just one win from seven league matches.

item.title: Medvedev defends Almaty Open title to close in on ATP Finals
item.description: Top seed Daniil Medvedev shook off a first-set stumble to beat Nikoloz Basilashvili 6-7(6) 6-1 6-3 to defend his Almaty Open title on Sunday, picking up his fourth trophy on the ATP Tour this year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Top seed Daniil Medvedev shook off a first-set stumble to beat Nikoloz Basilashvili 6-7(6) 6-1 6-3 to defend his Almaty Open title on Sunday, picking up his fourth trophy on the ATP Tour this year. The win was a boost for Medvedev's hopes of securing his place early in the ATP Finals, which he won in 2020. Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have already qualified for the tournament, while the injured Jannik Sinner will not feature in the eight-man season finale in Turin from November 15-22. "I always said, it's just a matter of luck, time, moment," said Medvedev after the first successful title defence of his career. "I was feeling fresh, I was feeling physically good... I'm happy to finally do it I guess," the 30-year-old added with a smile. Former US Open champion Medvedev saved two set points to force a tiebreak in the first set, but netted two attempted winners as qualifier Basilashvili, ranked 128th in the world, clinched the set with a powerful cross-court backhand. The world number five regained control in the second set, forcing backhand rallies and pressuring an error-prone Basilashvili into shooting wide. Georgian Basilashvili, playing in his first final on the tour since 2022, struggled with his nerves in the third set, netting a backhand drop shot to bring up Medvedev's first match point, before shooting wide from the baseline to lose the match. Medvedev is set to play in the Vienna Open starting on Monday, and the Paris Masters from October 31, as he looks to secure his place in Turin.

item.title: CON O Cuatro formas en que la política exterior de EEUU podría cambiar si demócratas ganan en noviembre
item.description: Analistas afirman que los demócratas tienen muchas posibilidades de ganar la Cámara de Representantes de Estados Unidos y, posiblemente, el Senado en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura de noviembre, lo que les otorgaría una parte del poder en Washington tras dos años de control republicano.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: Analistas afirman que los demócratas tienen muchas posibilidades de ganar la Cámara de Representantes de Estados Unidos y, posiblemente, el Senado en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura de noviembre, lo que les otorgaría una parte del poder en Washington tras dos años de control republicano. Los demócratas sostienen que los republicanos han permitido que el Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump declare la guerra y controle el gasto, a pesar de que la Constitución reserva esas competencias a los legisladores. A continuación se exponen algunas formas en las que un Congreso demócrata podría limitar la política exterior de Trump. FRENAR GUERRA CON IRÁN Trump no obtuvo aprobación del Congreso antes de iniciar la guerra con Irán el 28 de febrero, y los demócratas han votado en repetidas ocasiones a favor de poner fin a los combates a menos que lo haga. Una de estas resoluciones se aprobó con el apoyo de un puñado de republicanos, pero el Gobierno federal la ignoró. Con el control de la Cámara de Representantes o del Senado, los demócratas podrían recortar el gasto en defensa para presionar a Trump a fin de que obtenga el permiso del Congreso para continuar la guerra. También podrían exigir a los responsables del Gobierno que testifiquen públicamente sobre sus planes. NUEVO APOYO A UCRANIA Trump ha suspendido en gran medida la ayuda financiera y militar directa a Ucrania, a pesar del amplio apoyo de los legisladores demócratas y republicanos mientras este país se enfrenta a la invasión rusa. También ha enfurecido a miembros del Congreso, incluidos muchos republicanos, al levantar las sanciones al gasóleo ruso y eximir de sanciones a la energía rusa tan solo unas semanas después de promulgarlas como ley. Con una victoria en ambas cámaras en noviembre, los demócratas podrían decidir qué se somete a votación y cuándo. Esto les permitiría aprobar nuevas ayudas a Ucrania, que probablemente se aprobarían con la mayoría de dos tercios necesaria para superar un veto de Trump. También podrían actuar contra otras medidas de Trump. Gregory Meeks, —que podría presidir la Comisión de Asuntos Exteriores de la Cámara de Representantes si los demócratas obtienen el control—, ha presentado una propuesta de ley bipartidista para bloquear el plan de Trump de reintroducir el gasóleo ruso en el mercado mundial. PONER FIN A AYUDA MILITAR A ISRAEL El apoyo a Israel se ha desplomado entre los demócratas debido a su actuación en la guerra de Gaza, que ha causado la muerte de decenas de miles de civiles palestinos. La violencia que persiste en Cisjordania y la estrecha alianza del primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu con los republicanos también han sido factores determinantes. Los demócratas podrían limitar o poner fin a la ayuda militar a Israel, que ascendió a 3.800 millones de dólares en el último ejercicio fiscal. Esa cifra supera la ayuda proporcionada a cualquier otro país. Casi la mitad de los demócratas de la Cámara de Representantes votó este verano boreal a favor de suspender la ayuda a Israel. Algunos de los que votaron en contra de esa iniciativa, han respaldado la imposición de límites al suministro de armas, como bombas pesadas, a Israel. LIMITAR GASTO MILITAR Y RESTABLECER AYUDA EXTERIOR Los demócratas son mucho más propensos que los republicanos a limitar el gasto militar. Trump solicitó este año un aumento sin precedentes del 67% en el presupuesto militar, hasta 1,5 billones de dólares, pero los demócratas lo bloquearon en el Senado, alegando su negativa a consultar al Congreso sobre la guerra con Irán y sus drásticos recortes en los programas sociales. Trump también ha retenido o cancelado miles de millones de dólares en ayuda exterior aprobada por el Congreso. Muchos demócratas se han indignado por los recortes y afirman que intentarán restablecer la financiación.

item.title: Osaka says not far from best form despite retirement thoughts
item.description: Former world number one Naomi Osaka said she was close to rediscovering the form that brought her four Grand Slam titles, but acknowledged she had thought about retirement and often wondered how long she would continue playing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former world number one Naomi Osaka said she was close to rediscovering the form that brought her four Grand Slam titles, but acknowledged she had thought about retirement and often wondered how long she would continue playing. The 29-year-old Japanese, who stepped away from tennis for 15 months after the birth of her daughter before coming back in 2024, returns to the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo next week as the seventh seed. "It's tough, sometimes I look towards my future and wonder how long I'm going to play," Osaka told reporters on Sunday. "Because if my daughter did say she didn't want me to travel as much, I'm not the type of person to ignore that." Currently ranked 19th in the world, Osaka has shown signs of returning to her best this season, reaching the quarter-finals at Wimbledon after beating top seed Aryna Sabalenka and making the last 16 at both the French Open and US Open. She also reached the semi-finals in Washington and the quarter-finals in Toronto. "I genuinely don't feel like I'm that far off," Osaka said of her chances of contending for titles again. "I think I built a pretty solid base and I'm excited to see if I can continue learning and going further in tournaments." Osaka opens her Tokyo campaign against Italy's Jasmine Paolini, while world number one Elena Rybakina also headlines the field alongside Alex Eala of the Philippines.

item.title: Europa debería participar en las negociaciones de paz sobre Ucrania, afirma un asesor del Kremlin
item.description: Europa debería participar en las conversaciones sobre un acuerdo de paz en Ucrania, ya que su postura podría resultar crucial, afirmó el domingo Yuri Ushakov, asesor del Kremlin, quien destacó que Estados Unidos no ha sido capaz de presionar a Kiev para que acepte un pacto.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Europa debería participar en las conversaciones sobre un acuerdo de paz en Ucrania, ya que su postura podría resultar crucial, afirmó el domingo Yuri Ushakov, asesor del Kremlin, quien destacó que Estados Unidos no ha sido capaz de presionar a Kiev para que acepte un pacto. "Antes, tras la reunión de Anchorage, parecía que el Gobierno estadounidense podría dictar algo y obligar a Kiev a acatarlo. Pero, hasta ahora, eso no ha funcionado realmente", dijo Ushakov, refiriéndose a una reunión celebrada en 2025 en Anchorage entre el presidente estadounidense Donald Trump y su par ruso Vladimir Putin. "Esto se debe a que no basta con hablar solo con Kiev; tenemos que hablar con toda Europa, que apoya plenamente a Kiev", agregó en una entrevista con la TV estatal. Tras dejar inicialmente en manos de Trump la tarea de intentar negociar el fin de la guerra en Ucrania, la UE ha realizado acercamientos cautelosos a Rusia. Los líderes de Reino Unido, Alemania y Francia han manifestado su apoyo a una propuesta de conversaciones entre Volodimir Zelenski y Putin para intentar lograr un alto el fuego, y han señalado que Europa desempeñaría un papel en ello. Rusia, por su parte, ha declarado que estaría abierta al diálogo, pero no a los ultimátums. Ushakov afirmó que Moscú está dispuesto a reanudar las conversaciones de paz a tres bandas con Ucrania y Estados Unidos tras el Día de la Unidad Nacional de Rusia, el 4 de noviembre, haciéndose eco de los comentarios del Kremlin de esta semana sobre la disposición de Putin a reanudar las conversaciones con Ucrania, mediadas por Washington, el próximo mes. Zelenski declaró el viernes que los negociadores de paz de Ucrania, Rusia y Estados Unidos habían acordado reunirse a nivel técnico durante la primera quincena de noviembre en Abu Dabi, y añadió que esperaba que a ello le siguiera una reunión de sus líderes. Ushakov también se pronunció sobre una posible reunión entre Putin, el presidente chino Xi Jinping y Trump, y señaló que los preparativos ya habían comenzado. Está previsto que el encuentro se celebre al margen de la cumbre de la Cooperación Económica Asia-Pacífico (APEC), que tendrá lugar en China el 18 y 19 de noviembre. Según Ushakov, no se había acordado ninguna reunión por separado entre Putin y Trump en Shenzhen.

item.title: Arabia Saudita intercepta drones y misiles mientras continúan los combates con hutíes
item.description: Arabia Saudita interceptó el domingo drones y misiles sobre Riad y zonas del sur del país, informó la coalición liderada por el reino en Yemen, mientras continuaban los combates con los hutíes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Arabia Saudita interceptó el domingo drones y misiles sobre Riad y zonas del sur del país, informó la coalición liderada por el reino en Yemen, mientras continuaban los combates con los hutíes. El conflicto se ha convertido en un frente cada vez más desestabilizador en la ofensiva estadounidense-israelí contra Irán, lo que ha convertido a Arabia Saudita en un punto de presión en el contexto más amplio de la guerra. Las autoridades de defensa civil sauditas emitieron el domingo alertas de emergencia para Riad, Abha y Khamis Mushait, antes de anunciar, minutos después, que el peligro había pasado. La coalición afirmó que se lanzaron dos drones y un misil balístico hacia Riad, así como un misil de crucero hacia la ciudad meridional de Khamis Mushait. Posteriormente, señaló que había interceptado 10 misiles balísticos disparados hacia el sur de Arabia Saudita. Los hutíes advirtieron que podrían volver a atacar el Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Khalid de Riad, que reanudó el domingo sus operaciones en dos terminales tras una incursión a principios de este mes. Los hutíes afirmaron que el sábado atacaron el aeropuerto e instalaciones petroleras sauditas. Riad no se pronunció directamente sobre las declaraciones de los hutíes. El portavoz militar hutí, Yahya Saree, afirmó que el aeropuerto seguía siendo un "objetivo militar" y advirtió a todas las aerolíneas, al personal del aeropuerto y a los viajeros que no lo utilizaran. El aeropuerto suspendió sus operaciones el 10 de octubre tras un ataque —reivindicado por los hutíes— que causó la muerte de 13 personas y dejó más de 300 heridos, el más mortífero en el reino en una década. Riad intensificó sus ataques contra los hutíes después de que el grupo se hiciera con el control de territorio estratégico a lo largo de la costa del mar Rojo, acercándose al estrecho de Bab el-Mandeb —un punto estratégico marítimo mundial y ruta de transporte para los productores de petróleo del Golfo, en el lado opuesto de la península arábiga al estrecho de Ormuz-. La reanudación de los combates en Yemen ha hecho añicos una tregua negociada por la ONU que se había mantenido en gran medida desde 2022. Arabia Saudita intervino en la guerra civil de Yemen en 2015 al frente de una coalición que apoyaba al Gobierno reconocido internacionalmente, después de que los hutíes tomaran la capital, Saná, un año antes.

item.title: French protest groups demand more rallies as Macron faces tough choices
item.description: The government began talks with unions and student representatives to defuse the crisis, but protest leaders say the measures it has proposed are inadequate.
item.dc:creator: Crispian Balmer, Juliette Jabkhiro
item.content:encoded: French protest groups and unions called on Sunday for further demonstrations as they sought to maintain pressure on the government after a huge security operation helped to contain unrest during nationwide rallies on Saturday. The Interior Ministry said 410,000 people took part in Saturday's marches as authorities deployed 70,000 police, helping to avert a repeat of the looting and vandalism that swept many cities on October 17. Labour leaders urged further protests next Saturday and a nationwide strike on November 5, saying frustration over wages, living costs and public services was spreading far beyond the student movement that first mobilised last month. "We see an aggregation of anger," Murielle Guilbert, co-leader of the left-wing Solidaires trade union federation, told BFM TV. She said grievances from students, workers, firefighters and other groups were converging. "We call on people to take to the streets next Saturday." The SUD Education teaching union said it would join the October 31 demonstration while the large CGT union said it would decide during the week. MACRON'S SCOPE TO RESPOND IS MINIMAL The Yellow Vests, a grassroots movement that emerged in 2018 as a revolt against fuel taxes, also called for mass rallies next Saturday, including sit-ins outside town halls and the National Assembly. "There is anger in this country. It's growing in schools and universities, on roundabouts, in neighbourhoods, on farms and in workplaces," activist Azelma Sigaux told reporters. In 2019, President Emmanuel Macron was able to find the resources to reduce fuel costs in response to the Yellow Vests. Seven years on, strained public finances leave him with little room to meet protesters' demands. His mandate also expires next April and his centrist party no longer has the majority needed to pass major legislation. The government has begun talks with unions and student representatives to try to defuse the crisis, but protest leaders say the measures it has proposed so far are inadequate. "We have received no response at all from this government," said Guilbert. Police unions said on Sunday they did not have enough staff to maintain for any length of time the high level of deployment that on Saturday helped to limit disorder to sporadic clashes in a number of cities, including Paris and Marseille. Some 1,314 people were arrested on Saturday, half of last week's numbers, the interior ministry said on Sunday, and about 50 police were injured, compared with more than 1,000 last week. The protests have resonated beyond France's borders. On Saturday [USN:L6N46A05C TEXT:"Belgian police"] used tear gas and pepper spray as they clashed in Brussels with anti-government demonstrators. [USN:FWN4630JL TEXT:"In Albania"], peaceful protests that began at the end of May this month turned into violent unrest and skirmishes have taken place in several Italian cities for a second week running.

item.title: Anderson disappointed to see 25-year Lancashire journey come to an end
item.description: Fast bowler James Anderson expressed disappointment on Sunday after Lancashire decided not to renew his contract, bringing an end to a 25-year association between England's all-time leading test wicket-taker and his home county.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Fast bowler James Anderson expressed disappointment on Sunday after Lancashire decided not to renew his contract, bringing an end to a 25-year association between England's all-time leading test wicket-taker and his home county. Anderson, who claimed 704 test wickets for England, will leave Lancashire as the county look to move on from the 44-year-old and rebuild their squad for a promotion push from Division Two of the County Championship. The veteran bowler made 112 first-class appearances for Lancashire, claiming 443 wickets, and was involved in their County Championship title triumph in 2011. "I've supported Lancashire since I was a kid, and so to get to play for them for 25 years was a dream come true," Anderson said in a statement. "I have always found it special walking out to play at Old Trafford and have some incredible memories of doing so including the honour of being captain. "If it was up to me it wouldn't have ended like this but I wish the players and fans all the best for the future." Anderson, who was appointed Lancashire's red-ball captain for the first time in his career in the 2026 season, took 50 wickets at an average of 17.68 this summer, but the county finished seventh out of eight teams in the second division. "I spoke to Jimmy about our ambitions to rebuild our men's squad that is capable of securing promotion from Division Two of the County Championship and then challenging to win Division One over the next three to four years," said Paul Farbrace, Lancashire's incoming director of cricket. "We are keen to begin that rebuild now, both in terms of the playing squad and the wider professional cricket set-up, and to make important progress over the coming months. "As part of those plans, I informed Jimmy that we had taken the incredibly difficult decision not to extend his playing contract for the 2027 season." Lancashire Cricket had honoured Anderson's contribution to the club by renaming the Pavilion End at Old Trafford the James Anderson End. He was also knighted in 2025 in recognition of his services to cricket.

item.title: Grupo trabajadores advierte de importantes pérdidas de puestos de trabajo en Suiza si UBS se traslada
item.description: Hasta 12.000 puestos de trabajo de UBS en Suiza podrían verse amenazados si unas normas de capital más estrictas obligaran al banco a trasladarse, dijo la Asociación Suiza de Empleados Bancarios (SBPV).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hasta 12.000 puestos de trabajo de UBS (UBSG.S) en Suiza podrían verse amenazados si unas normas de capital más estrictas obligaran al banco a trasladarse, dijo la Asociación Suiza de Empleados Bancarios (SBPV). En una carta dirigida a los legisladores y publicada por primera vez el fin de semana por el periódico NZZ am Sonntag, la asociación advirtió que una relocalización, venta o fusión de UBS podría suponer la pérdida de entre 10.000 y 12.000 de los aproximadamente 34.000 puestos de trabajo de UBS en Suiza. La carta, a la que también tuvo acceso Reuters, describía esta situación como el "peor de los casos" y se suma a los recortes ya realizados en el banco mientras completa la integración de Credit Suisse, que adquirió en 2023. UBS, que ha afirmado en repetidas ocasiones que quiere permanecer en Suiza, se negó a comentar la estimación de la SBPV. Un portavoz de UBS afirmó que el banco mantendría al mínimo posible los recortes de empleo derivados de la adquisición de Credit Suisse. UBS ha señalado que sigue previendo unos 3.000 despidos en Suiza como consecuencia de la integración y que estos se producirían a lo largo de varios años, principalmente a través de medidas como la rotación natural de personal, las jubilaciones anticipadas y la internalización de puestos de trabajo que antes se realizaban de forma externa. La advertencia de la SBPV se produce mientras una comisión de la cámara baja del Parlamento suizo se dispone a debatir cuánto capital debería mantener UBS para respaldar a sus filiales extranjeras. El mes pasado, la cámara alta propuso que UBS respaldara esas unidades con un 90% de capital ordinario de nivel 1 (CET1). UBS ha sugerido que esa cifra es excesiva y el presidente del banco ha advertido que tendría que plantearse cuidadosamente su futuro en Suiza si las normas resultaran demasiado estrictas. Algunos accionistas han pedido que UBS abandone Suiza, y el banco ha estado elaborando posibles planes de contingencia, entre los que se incluyen el traslado de su sede o la fusión con otra entidad crediticia, dijeron fuentes a Reuters.

item.title: Viceprimer ministro dice Rusia está dispuesta a suministrar a EEUU cualquier cantidad de diesel: TV estatal
item.description: El viceprimer ministro ruso, Alexander Novak, afirmó que Rusia está dispuesta a suministrar a Estados Unidos cualquier cantidad de gasóleo, informó el domingo el canal de televisión estatal
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El viceprimer ministro ruso, Alexander Novak, afirmó que Rusia está dispuesta a suministrar a Estados Unidos cualquier cantidad de gasóleo, informó el domingo el canal de televisión estatal Vesti. "Todo lo que nuestros socios quieran (...) del volumen total que vamos a exportar. Podemos suministrarlo todo", afirmó Novak en una entrevista. Novak había declarado el viernes que tres petroleros cargados con gasóleo ruso se dirigían a Norteamérica.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vota no Rio e faz apelo para que eleitores compareçam às urnas
item.description: O candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) votou nesta manhã de domingo em uma escola em Vila Isabel, no Rio de Janeiro, e, em breve declaração à imprensa, fez um apelo aos eleitores para que compareçam às urnas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) votou nesta manhã de domingo em uma escola em Vila Isabel, no Rio de Janeiro, e, em breve declaração à imprensa, fez um apelo aos eleitores para que compareçam às urnas. "Faça chuva ou faça sol, bora sair de casa para votar, que o Brasil vai mudar e o Brasil vai vencer", disse o senador. A previsão de chuvas fortes em algumas regiões do país neste domingo tem alimentado a preocupação de aumento da abstenção eleitoral neste segundo turno entre Flávio Bolsonaro e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). "Chegou a hora da mudança de verdade", afirmou o candidato, ao lado da esposa Fernanda e da mãe, Rogéria, comemorando o que disse ter sido uma campanha "leve" e "limpa" para o segundo turno. "Eu vim com propostas mostrando que a gente tem toda a condição de montar um grande time para reorganizar o Brasil", declarou.

item.title: Brasileños eligen entre Lula y Flávio Bolsonaro en balotaje presidencial
item.description: Los brasileños votaban el domingo en una reñida segunda vuelta electoral que podría inclinar bruscamente a la derecha a la nación más grande de América Latina, acercándola a Estados Unidos como parte de un giro conservador más amplio en toda la región.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin
item.content:encoded: Los brasileños votaban el domingo en una reñida segunda vuelta electoral que podría inclinar bruscamente a la derecha a la nación más grande de América Latina, acercándola a Estados Unidos como parte de un giro conservador más amplio en toda la región. La segunda vuelta enfrenta al presidente izquierdista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva con el senador derechista Flávio Bolsonaro. El hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro dio la sorpresa a principios de mes al liderar la votación en la primera vuelta en contra de lo que decían las encuestas. Un triunfo de Bolsonaro, de 45 años, prolongaría la ola de victorias de la derecha para los candidatos latinoamericanos afines a Donald Trump, mientras que un cuarto mandato para Lula sería una decepción en Washington, que ha tenido roces con su gobierno en materia de comercio y seguridad. Reuters reveló el sábado una campaña dentro del Departamento de Estado de Trump para ayudar a que los Bolsonaro volvieran al poder. La contienda electoral ha estado marcada por escándalos de corrupción, incertidumbre económica y acusaciones de injerencia estadounidense, algo que Washington niega. También se ha visto influenciada por las repercusiones de la condena de Jair Bolsonaro en 2025 por planear un golpe de Estado en 2022, ante la promesa de Flávio de liberar a su padre si resulta elegido. Trump calificó el caso de "caza de brujas" e impuso un arancel del 50% a Brasil en 2025, en una decisión vinculada explícitamente al juicio de Jair Bolsonaro. Si bien muchas de estas medidas fueron posteriormente suavizadas, el mandatario republicano impuso nuevos aranceles a Brasil este año, alegando prácticas comerciales desleales. Lula ha presentado la cercanía del Gobierno de Trump con el clan Bolsonaro como parte de un intento de influir en las elecciones, al tiempo que ha calificado los aranceles y otras medidas punitivas de intimidación. En materia económica, a pesar de la disminución de la desigualdad y el desempleo, Lula ha tenido dificultades para ganarse a un electorado que lidia con el alto costo de la vida y las elevadas deudas familiares. La violencia endémica de las pandillas también preocupa a los votantes. Bolsonaro ha intentado sacar provecho de la preocupación por el costo de la vida y también ha prometido mano dura para combatir la delincuencia, comprometiéndose a construir cárceles de máxima seguridad y a aplicar la castración química para los delitos sexuales graves. Al emitir su voto en Río de Janeiro el domingo, Flávio Bolsonaro instó a la gente a acudir a las urnas "con lluvia o con sol". Lula, por su parte, votará en São Bernardo do Campo, cerca de São Paulo. RESULTADO INCIERTO Las encuestas muestran que los candidatos están prácticamente empatados de cara a la segunda vuelta, con recortando distancias en los últimos días. Sin embargo, los precedentes históricos favorecen a Bolsonaro, ya que ningún candidato ha ganado la presidencia tras quedar segundo en la primera vuelta de las elecciones. Bolsonaro obtuvo el 47% de los votos emitidos en la primera vuelta, contra e 45% de Lula. La victoria del senador disparó los mercados brasileños y su moneda ante las expectativas de reformas favorables a las empresas. Su éxito en la primera vuelta se vio reflejado en las elecciones al Congreso de su Partido Liberal y de otros políticos de derecha, lo que podría allanarle el camino legislativo o complicarle la gobernabilidad a Lula.

item.title: Conservative party wins first election in nearly a century in British Columbia
item.description: The opposition Conservative Party won an election in the Canadian province of British Columbia for the first time in nearly 100 years, promising to ramp up liquefied natural gas production, provisional results showed on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The opposition Conservative Party won an election in the Canadian province of British Columbia for the first time in nearly 100 years, promising to ramp up liquefied natural gas production, provisional results showed on Sunday. The result marks an end to nine years of power for the left-of-center New Democrats, who voiced opposition to new oil pipelines and supported a ban on tankers along the province's northern coast The right-leaning Conservatives won 64 of the 93 seats and the New Democrats won 27. It is the first Conservative provincial election win since 1928 The Conservatives pledged to double natural gas production by 2032 and more than triple it by 2035 "I believe in energy... We will cut red tape like it's never been cut before," Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson said in his victory speech Doerkson, who will become the next premier of the province, promised to "supercharge" BC. The province will host a business summit in Vancouver next year The Conservatives promised to end emissions limits, replace the province's carbon tax framework and reach out to energy providers that had left the province's LNG sector since 2018, including ExxonMobil, Chevron and Woodside Polls showed voters were focused on cost-of-living issues, healthcare, and the ongoing trade war with US President Donald Trump New Democrat Premier David Eby had called for a strong mandate to confront Trump's tariff threats

item.title: Netanyahu rebuked for plan to use crypto to bypass economic sanctions
item.description: His comments drew a rare rebuke by the Bank of Israel.
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces [USN:L8N45Y0MD TEXT:"re-election"] this week, is drawing criticism from economists and political rivals after suggesting Israel could use cryptocurrency to help shield its economy from potential international sanctions. In an interview with Israel's Channel 10 on Friday, Netanyahu said he was preparing for a scenario in which broader sanctions were imposed on Israel. Last month, Britain, France and Canada said they would [USN:S8N42N05Y TEXT:"block imports"] from Israeli settlements in the West Bank in what was the latest in a series of actions targeting Israel's settlement policy, underscoring its growing diplomatic isolation among some of its traditional allies. "There could be sanctions, and sanctions on banks so you need to set up a bypass economy," Netanyahu said. "You know, there are currencies that can bypass (sanctions). We are also working on that." Asked whether he was referring to cryptocurrency, Netanyahu replied: "Very true, very true," adding that blockchain technology was another possibility. The comments drew a rare rebuke by the Bank of Israel, which said crypto currencies cannot serve as a route to bypass sanctions and that political leaders should focus on policy that would render such measures unnecessary. "The right course for Israel's economy is to preserve our economic relations with our main trading partners, and to focus on preventing sanctions and their negative impact on the economy," it said. Netanyahu on Sunday continued to defend his record, urging voters to back him and saying he and US President Donald Trump had two years left to work together to topple Iran's rulers . PLAN DRAWS CRITICISM On Sunday, more than 100 economists, including former Bank of Israel officials, ex-central bank governor Jacob Frenkel and several Nobel laureates, signed a letter expressing alarm over Netanyahu's proposal. They said it would lead to higher unemployment, a fall in foreign investment and the collapse of Israel's economic standing in the world. "As we have seen in countries that have suffered similar sanctions, such as South Africa, Iran, and Russia, the living standards of Israeli citizens would plummet dramatically, and the state's ability to finance its security and defend itself against its enemies would be severely damaged," the letter read. "Netanyahu is knowingly leading the State of Israel toward boycott and international economic isolation, and all he has to offer the Israeli economy is a puzzling solution, one accepted in criminal organizations, that will not help in the slightest." Netanyahu's main rival in Tuesday's election, [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Gadi Eisenkot"], called the crypto plan "madness" and said he feared that the "BibiCoin policy" would drive companies abroad and undermine national security. Opposition leader Yair Lapid said: "Netanyahu has gone off the rails ... He promises the citizens of Israel before these elections that they'll be standing in line for an hour and a half for bread, like in Russia and Iran." Opinion polls point to a potential stalemate in the election with neither Netanyahu's ruling coalition nor an opposition alliance securing a governing majority in parliament.

item.title: British pin hopes of late SailGP lift on training blitz
item.description: Britain have struggled off the start line this season but the defending champions were the first to grab a week of intensive training at SailGP's new performance facility as they pursue a Grand Final berth, skipper Dylan Fletcher said.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Smith
item.content:encoded: Britain have struggled off the start line this season but the defending champions were the first to grab a week of intensive training at SailGP's new performance facility as they pursue a Grand Final berth, skipper Dylan Fletcher said. With only two events left, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi next month, the British are fifth in the championship, just behind the US and Sweden, in pursuit of a top-three finish that would earn a place in the winner-takes-all Grand Final. "We put our name down early to get one of these slots and I think that it's a really good opportunity," Fletcher told Reuters at the start of a week practising in Pensacola, Florida. SailGP gives crews very little practice on board their F50 catamarans, which can hit more than 100 kph when they lift above the water on foils, a gap the new facility aims to bridge. "We haven't had the season that we've been happy with at the moment. And this in reality feels like a great opportunity, not just on the water, but off the water," said Fletcher, ahead of the team's first 2-1/2-hour F50 session. "We're mainly focused on light wind starting... We've seen that as much as we've been still quite good at overtaking, the reality is it's all about the start," said Fletcher. "The Aussies have been the standout performers and you know that shows," he added of how the season's leaders start. The British are seeking short-term gains with their week in Pensacola, which can offer the lighter wind conditions that are the norm in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, as well as looking ahead to next season, which starts in Hong Kong in January. "We want to try and finish this season strong regardless of how it goes... to start off on the right foot (next season) because we obviously haven't been sailing at the level that we expect," Fletcher said. Despite the team's dip in form, Fletcher has not given up. "If we sail well enough to win the Grand Final, then we will be in the Grand Final. The momentum is almost more important going into those last two events," the 38-year-old said. "If you look at how the results generally go, I'd say if we made the final in both (Dubai and Abu Dhabi), it would be surprising if we weren't in the Grand Final," he added. While Spain's Los Gallos have "pretty much qualified", they have "everything to lose", Fletcher said, adding that the "British underdogs" had "absolutely nothing to lose". The British are focusing particularly on the pre-start "trigger" manoeuvre used to make sure the boat hits the line at top speed, along with Fletcher's positioning on the course. "We're going to try and execute that and have a bit of a change in our strategy," Fletcher said, adding: "Hopefully we can just tip the scales back in our favour, and we'll be away and looking like the team that we know we can be."

item.title: Rybakina brushes aside Fernandez to retain Ningbo crown
item.description: Elena Rybakina blazed past unseeded Canadian Leylah Fernandez 6-2 6-2 to retain her Ningbo Open title and lift her first trophy as the world number one ahead of the WTA Finals next month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Elena Rybakina blazed past unseeded Canadian Leylah Fernandez 6-2 6-2 in the Ningbo Open final on Sunday to retain her title and lift her first trophy as the world number one ahead of the WTA Finals next month. The victory in Ningbo also helped the Kazakh to take a big step towards securing the year-end number one ranking, further burnishing a spectacular season in which she won the Australian Open title before adding the US Open crown to reach the summit. "It's amazing to play in front of you... it's my second year here and my second win," Rybakina told the crowd in the eastern Chinese city after collecting a tour-leading fourth title of the season and 15th overall. "It's such a special place for me. Thanks so much Ningbo." Rybakina's latest triumph is a timely lift after setbacks in Beijing and Wuhan, as she turns her attention to the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo this week before she launches her title defence at the season finale in Indian Wells, California, from November 8. TRADEMARK POWER Top seed Rybakina made the breakthrough with her trademark power in the fifth game and then unleashed a searing crosscourt backhand winner to go 4-2 up, before the 27-year-old wrapped up the opening set in 38 minutes. World number 30 Fernandez made a bright start to the next set but Rybakina absorbed the pressure and raised her level to force an error and break for 2-1, with the three-times Grand Slam champion breezing to victory from there. Fernandez, who won the Singapore Open last month, remained upbeat despite a disappointing showing in the final and backed herself to finish the season strongly after a gruelling run of matches in Ningbo. "I'd like to congratulate Elena for a wonderful week and a wonderful year. Congratulations to you and your team," the 24-year-old said, before addressing her own team. "We're having a good end of year. We've just got to keep going and keep working hard."

item.title: Serbia election: Main players, voter concerns and what is at stake
item.description: Serbia is holding parliamentary elections on Sunday, in which a popular student movement is seeking to end the rule of longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic.
item.dc:creator: Canan Sevgili, Arda Dipova, Ivana Sekularac
item.content:encoded: Serbia is holding [USN:L6N46B017 TEXT:"parliamentary elections"] on Sunday, in which a popular student movement is seeking to end the rule of longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic. Here are the main players, issues and stakes in the vote. WHO ARE THE MAJOR PLAYERS AND WHAT DO THEY STAND FOR? Aleksandar Vucic – United Serbia: The Serbian Progressive Party (SNS)-led electoral list is campaigning on economic growth, higher wages and pensions, infrastructure investment and political stability. SNS leader Milos Vucevic has pledged 4% economic growth in 2027. Vucic, who resigned as president on September 27, is running to become prime minister. Students Win: Emerging from protests over the November 2024 Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse that killed 16 people, the anti-corruption movement has campaigned for accountability and transparent public procurement. The Democratic Party and Kreni Promeni movement have backed it rather than fielding their own lists. Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) – Ivica Dacic – Factor of Stability: A longstanding ally of the SNS, the pro-Russian SPS leads a coalition with Unified Serbia, the Social Democratic Party of Serbia and the Greens of Serbia. It campaigns on social justice, workers' rights and welfare, political stability, and national interests. European Serbia: A pro-European opposition alliance led by Marinika Tepic and Zdravko Ponos, bringing together the Party of Freedom and Justice, Serbia Centre, and the Solidarity, Self-Defence and Liberation movement. It advocates closer European integration, sanctions against Russia and democratic reforms. WHAT ARE PARTY LISTS AND HOW DO THEY WORK? Political parties, party coalitions, movements and other groups can submit party lists, or electoral lists comprising no more than 250 candidates.
