The election commission has approved a total of 18 lists. On election day, voters vote for one electoral list on the ballot, rather than individual candidates. WHAT ARE THE MAIN ISSUES FOR VOTERS? Corruption and government accountability have dominated the campaign since the Novi Sad disaster. Protesters accuse Vucic and his allies of corruption, controlling the media and mistreating demonstrators, allegations the authorities deny. Living standards, economic development and the fairness of the electoral process are also campaign issues. HOW WILL A VICTORY OR LOSS FOR VUCIC IMPACT SERBIA AT HOME AND ABROAD? A victory allowing Vucic to become prime minister would extend his political leadership and could preserve Serbia's balancing act between its ambition to join the European Union and maintain Belgrade's close ties with Russia and China. A defeat could pave the way for sweeping domestic reforms, including stronger institutions and measures against corruption.

item.title: Flávio e Lula disputam Presidência em eleição que pode ser definida pela abstenção
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) decidem neste domingo quem governará o Brasil a partir de 5 de janeiro de 2027 após uma das campanhas eleitorais mais tensas e recheadas de acusações da história da política brasileira, sem que as pesquisas apontem um favorito claro e com um provável papel decisivo do comparecimento dos eleitores às urnas.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Simões
item.content:encoded: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) decidem neste domingo quem governará o Brasil a partir de 5 de janeiro de 2027 após uma das campanhas eleitorais mais tensas e recheadas de acusações da história da política brasileira, sem que as pesquisas apontem um favorito claro e com um provável papel decisivo do comparecimento dos eleitores às urnas. Senador de oposição e filho mais velho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio, de 45 anos, largou na frente após um resultado surpreendente no primeiro turno, disputado há três semanas, quando terminou na liderança com 47,03% dos votos, contra 45,16% de Lula. O atual presidente e candidato à reeleição, que completará 81 anos na próxima terça e que busca um quarto mandato presidencial, reduziu gradativamente a distância para o rival nas pesquisas de intenção de voto mais recentes, o que leva a corrida a um cenário incerto. “O que o povo fez comigo nesses dias é uma coisa que não tem como pagar, é muita generosidade, é muito carinho, é muito amor e eu serei eternamente grato ao comportamento do povo”, disse o petista a jornalistas após votar na manhã deste domingo, em São Bernardo do Campo (SP), berço político do Partido dos Trabalhadores. As [USN:L2N46A047 TEXT:"pesquisas divulgadas na véspera"] da votação deste domingo mostraram um empate técnico com vantagem numérica de Flávio sobre Lula de no máximo dois pontos nos votos válidos, com 51% a 49%. "Flávio é ligeiramente favorito, ele não é francamente favorito", disse o cientista político Carlos Melo, do Insper. "Quando você olha para as pesquisas, mais do que o número você tem que olhar para a tendência. A tendência é o Flávio caindo, ou praticamente paralisado, e o Lula subindo muito devagar", acrescentou, apontando que não é possível prever se essa tendência resultará em uma virada a favor de Lula neste domingo. Um dos fatores cruciais a ser observado, na avaliação de Melo, será o comparecimento às urnas, já que historicamente o eleitorado que tende a apoiar mais Lula e o PT costuma ter um comparecimento menor. Não à toa, a campanha de Lula vem concentrando esforços em incentivar pessoas que não votaram no primeiro turno a comparecerem na seção eleitoral neste domingo. No primeiro turno, mais de 33,4 milhões de eleitores não foram votar, uma abstenção de 21,08%, em um total de mais de 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar. Neste domingo, no entanto, foi Flávio Bolsonaro quem fez um apelo para que os eleitores compareçam às urnas. "Faça chuva ou faça sol, bora sair de casa para votar, que o Brasil vai mudar e o Brasil vai vencer", disse o senador, após votar no Rio de Janeiro. "Chegou a hora da mudança de verdade", afirmou o candidato, ao lado da esposa Fernanda e da mãe, Rogéria. As três semanas de campanha do segundo turno foram bastante diferentes dos meses que antecederam o primeiro turno, realizado no dia 4 de outubro. No caso de Lula, uma guinada em direção a uma mobilização maciça nas redes sociais e em eventos de rua, que ocorreu sem participação direta do núcleo duro da campanha no primeiro turno, contrastou com uma primeira fase de campanha que o próprio Lula reconheceu em reunião do PT como a "menos organizada" de que participou desde 1989. Na véspera da eleição, antes de participar de evento de campanha em Copacabana, Lula afirmou que "o povo assumiu para si a responsabilidade de fazer a campanha". Um dos destaques da campanha petista no segundo turno foi o impulso nas redes, liderada pelo canal de WhatsApp "Exército do Lula", criado pelo deputado federal reeleito André Janones (Rede-MG), que juntou mais de 10 milhões de pessoas para ouvir as "missões" que Janones dá para os apoiadores cumprirem nas redes. A campanha de Flávio chegou a entrar no TSE pedindo a suspensão do canal. A guinada digital da campanha petista teve como ápice Lula, um crítico público do uso frequente de celular que se orgulhava de não ter o aparelho, ganhando um de presente do governador reeleito do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles (PT), e passando a fazer vários vídeos no formato selfie para apoiadores. Do lado de Flávio, após a inesperada liderança no dia 4, o senador deu declarações que geraram polêmica, como quando disse que, se eleito, usará a força que terá no próximo Congresso para alterar a Constituição. Posteriormente, afirmou que iria propor mudanças constitucionais como o fim da reeleição e a redução da maioridade penal. Também acabou mudando de posição em temas pautados por Lula, como o fim da escala de trabalho 6x1, ao qual ele votou a favor no Senado, apesar de, num passado muito recente, ter se declarado contrário. O senador, por outro lado, também conseguiu mobilizar grandes públicos em atos de campanha em todo o país, no que foi uma marca da campanha de ambos os lados. Na véspera da eleição, e em meio à previsão de chuvas fortes nas regiões Sul e Sudeste, onde Flávio teve desempenho melhor que Lula, o senador usou suas redes sociais para incentivar as pessoas a irem votar. "Pega alguém que não foi votar no primeiro turno e leva para votar no segundo. Compareça às urnas neste segundo turno, independente do tempo, faça chuva, faça sol, não deixe de sair de casa para votar, cada voto é muito importante", afirmou ele em vídeo publicado em sua conta no Instagram. JUDICIALIZAÇÃO Em uma campanha marcada por grande movimentação das duas campanhas contra os adversários no TSE, que levou o presidente da corte Kassio Nunes Marques, a pedir que as campanhas moderassem a quantidade de ações, há receios de que, independentemente do vencedor, ocorram novos embates mesmo após a declaração do resultado. A expectativa de uma margem apertada a favor do eleito também leva a crer que isso possa ocorrer. "A expectativa é de que vai ser uma eleição tensa", disse Creomar de Souza, analista político da Dharma Political Risk. "Acho que a gente ainda vai ter algum nível de discussão política, algum nível de embate jurídico", avaliou. Tanto Flávio quanto Lula não hesitaram em se acusar mutuamente de ladrão, corrupto e mentiroso ao longo de uma campanha em que propostas e discussões sobre o país ficaram em segundo plano. Denúncias de irregularidades contra os candidatos e seus familiares foram amplamente explorados, levando, nos últimos dias, a uma guerra de narrativas sobre a abertura de sigilos das duas partes. Em uma eleição que mais uma vez marcou a importância das redes sociais no processo político, a Meta (META.O) , proprietária do Facebook, do Instagram e do WhatsApp também ficou no foco, após a campanha de Lula apontar que teve sua atuação restrita nas plataformas da empresa, levando a big tech norte-americana a prestar esclarecimentos ao TSE.

item.title: Uganda to impose 21-day quarantine on returning citizens with Congo travel history
item.description: Ugandan citizens returning to the country with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of Congo will be quarantined for 21 days, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said on Sunday as Uganda tightened Ebola precautions despite saying it remained Ebola-free.
item.dc:creator: Elias Biryabarema
item.content:encoded: Ugandan citizens returning to the country with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of Congo will be quarantined for 21 days, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said on Sunday as Uganda tightened Ebola precautions despite saying it remained Ebola-free. Uganda has been investigating a Nigerian Ebola case involving a woman who had travelled from Uganda. Officials said they were reviewing genomic sequencing, travel information, interactions and movements in coordination with Nigerian authorities and international partners. Baryomunsi said on Sunday that all 60 contacts linked to a [USN:L6N469174 TEXT:"Kenyan Ebola case"] had completed their 21-day monitoring period and been discharged. The contacts were traced across points of entry and exit, hotels and transport operators linked to travellers' movements through Uganda. "The ministry has intensified traveller screening at Entebbe International Airport and all land border crossings. All travellers intending to enter Uganda by air, land or water must complete the passenger locator form," he said. [USN:L1N46915U TEXT:"Genomic analysis"] of Nigeria's only confirmed Ebola case showed the virus was closely related to the strain detected in Kenya's index case, though Nigerian authorities said there was no evidence that the Kenya case travelled to Nigeria or had a direct connection. Uganda borders Congo, where the outbreak began, and has previously battled Ebola outbreaks.

item.title: Real Madrid goalkeeper Courtois to miss Clasico due to illness
item.description: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss his side's LaLiga fixture at Barcelona on Sunday due to the flu, the club said in a statement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss his side's LaLiga fixture at Barcelona on Sunday due to the flu, the club said in a statement. Courtois' absence leaves manager Jose Mourinho without a key player for a vital clash with their league-leading rivals. The 34-year-old Belgian will miss his first game this season. Andriy Lunin is in line to replace Courtois in goal at Camp Nou. Lunin's last appearance for Real Madrid came on May 3, in a 2-0 win over Espanyol. Illia Voloshyn has been called up to the senior squad, with Sergio Mestre the other goalkeeper in the matchday squad.

item.title: Newlands to provide test of more than bat and ball for Australia
item.description: The third test will be held at the scene of the Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal.
item.dc:creator: Nick Said
item.content:encoded: Australia return to the scene of one of the darkest days in the country’s cricket history when the series-deciding third test against South Africa starts at Newlands on Tuesday. The battle may be mental as much as one of skill for several of the Australian players, not least former captain Steve Smith, who was at the centre of the Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal in 2018. Current skipper Pat Cummins was part of that side, as were fellow seamer Josh Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon, though they say they had no knowledge of the attempt to alter the condition of the ball with a piece of sandpaper. Smith bore the brunt of the considerable fallout in Australia eight years ago and having not reached the heights he might have expected on this tour, averaging a little over 20 with the bat, he would see this as the perfect time to put that right. There has so far been little chatter in South Africa about Sandpapergate but that could change at Newlands, where the first three days’ ticket sales have been strong after sparse crowds at the first two tests in Durban and Gqeberha. "He'll be fine," Australia opener Travis Head said of Smith. "I think he showed that in 2019 in England. We support him. He's been through a lot in that space and handles it well. Sometimes it brings the best out of him, as we've seen in the past." The series is level at 1-1 after big wins for both sides in the opening two games and Australia wicketkeeper Alex Carey told reporters on Sunday that it looked to be another good test-match pitch. "We are still a couple of days out but it looks another great surface," he said. "If you look back at Durban it was a five-day test match and a great contest between bat and ball. The same in Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha) and this should be no different." There has never been a test match played at Newlands in October, and just three in November, all against Australia. The tourists won the first two in 1902 and 1921, but the most recent November fixture was an eight-wicket victory for South Africa in 2011 when Australia were famously bowled out for 47 in their second innings. South Africa will be without fast bowler Anrich Nortje, who injured his groin in the second test. Captain Temba Bavuma said they would pick horses for courses in terms of his replacement. "You’ve got guys like Gerald (Coetzee), Pato (Dane Paterson), as well as (Corbin) Bosch, and we have Sen (Senuran Muthusamy) as well, so the options are there," he said. "Whoever we decide, we’ll be confident they form part of our best XI for the conditions."

item.title: Pacers expect more of themselves, look to regroup vs. winless Nets
item.description: Getting a win in guard Tyrese Haliburton's return to the court was emotional and joyful, but the follow-up was a massive letdown for the Indiana Pacers, especially in the opening 24 minutes.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Getting a win in guard Tyrese Haliburton's return to the court was emotional and joyful, but the follow-up was a massive letdown for the Indiana Pacers, especially in the opening 24 minutes. Two nights after getting outclassed in the first half, the Pacers hope their performance is vastly improved Sunday night when they visit the winless Brooklyn Nets. Haliburton has scored 41 points and handed out 19 assists in his first two games after missing all of last season with a torn right Achilles tendon. The star point guard returned with a double-double during a 123-120 win in the season opener at New Orleans before scoring 18 in Friday's 121-105 loss to the Dallas Mavericks in Indiana's home opener. While the final margin was only 16 points, the Pacers were much worse in the opening half. Indiana allowed 77 points in the first half and trailed by as many as 37. Against New Orleans, Indiana allowed 66 points in the first half. Through two games, the Pacers have been outscored by 44 points before halftime. "It just simply comes down to an attitude and a disposition," Pacers coach Rick Carlisle said. "And two straight games, we haven't had it the way we need to have it in the first half. "It's not OK, and we all own it. Every single one of us. Start with me. I didn't have these guys ready to play the way they needed to be ready to play." Indiana is hoping to avoid giving up 44 points in the first quarter like it did on Friday when Dallas wound up shooting 69.6% from the floor (16 of 23) and hitting 8 of 13 3-point tries (61.5%). "There's obviously a lot of room for us to grow," Haliburton said. "We've got to be better. And I really put it on that first five. We've got to be a lot better in that starting group." Forward Pascal Siakam led the Pacers with 23 points after getting 30 in the season opener, but Indiana would like more consistency from center Ivica Zubac, who was held to nine after getting 16 in the season opener. The Nets are trying to avoid losing their first three games for the second straight season. Last season, the Nets lost their first three by a combined 37 points as part of a seven-game skid en route to a 62-loss season. Brooklyn's two losses are by a combined 11 points, and the Nets nearly erased a 22-point deficit in Saturday's 125-121 loss at Cleveland. Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle have been Brooklyn's leading scorers in each game and are hoping to see more help like the duo got in the second half. Porter led the Nets with 28 points and Randle added 23 while second-year guard Egor Demin contributed 15 of his 22 points in the fourth quarter. Brooklyn scored 41 points and hit nine of its 16 3-point attempts in the fourth. "I think it was the shot quality," Nets coach Jordi Fernandez said. "We went from taking 35 good shots in the first half to almost 50 in the second. When you take the high-quality shots, they don't all go in at the same time, but then if you keep shooting them, we had that stretch that they kept going in." The Nets will likely have a slightly different lineup because rookie Mikel Brown Jr. will sit on the second night of a back-to-back. Brown shot 3-for-10, scored eight points in 20 minutes and shared the court with Demin in the fourth. But the guard, the sixth overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, also dealt with an ankle issue in the preseason and is on a minutes restriction. --Field Level Media

item.title: Senegal party that controls parliament comes out against revised budget bill
item.description: Senegal's Pastef party, which holds a large majority in the National Assembly, said it would not pass the government's revised budget, reinforcing doubts over how quickly the country can push ahead with its debt restructuring.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Senegal's Pastef party, which holds a large majority in the National Assembly, said it would not pass the government's revised budget, reinforcing doubts over how quickly the country can push ahead with its debt restructuring . A statement by the party headed by former Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko cited "disagreements over certain budgetary decisions, the chosen financing arrangements and the insufficient guarantees provided to parliament", though it said the party was open to engaging with the government on getting a new budget in place The West African nation has been grappling with a debt burden that had reached 132% of gross domestic product by the end of 2024, International Monetary Fund figures show, after the government uncovered billions of dollars in [USN:L8N3TJ1N8 TEXT:"misreported borrowing"] by the previous administration The government reached a staff-level agreement with the IMF in early September for a $2.2 billion, 36-month Extended Credit Facility to support its reform program. But without parliamentary approval of the revised budget, the government risks delaying the IMF program, which underpins its entire debt restructuring strategy Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo plans to hold a press conference on Sunday to discuss the revised budget "which is intended to implement a revised framework aimed at improving the quality of life of Senegalese people" The amended 2026 budget bill paints a sharply deteriorating fiscal picture. It cuts real GDP growth to 2.7% from roughly 5% in the original budget and widens the deficit to 7.6% of GDP from 5.4%, driven largely by a tripling of energy subsidies to 790.3 billion CFA francs ($1.36 billion) from 250 billion

item.title: Beirut's $13 chicken sandwich becomes symbol of Lebanon divide
item.description: Seven years after Lebanon’s devastating financial meltdown, a debate over a chicken sandwich has exposed an increasingly stark divide between those who can still spend freely and those struggling to get by.
item.dc:creator: Nazih Osseiran, Raghed Waked, Emilie Madi
item.content:encoded: Seven years after Lebanon’s [USN:L6N41Y0N8 TEXT:"devastating financial meltdown"], a debate over a chicken sandwich has exposed an increasingly stark divide between those who can still spend freely and those struggling to get by. A trendy health restaurant wanted to offer its calorie-conscious customers a healthier take on the beloved Levantine wrap known as the shish taouk. So, The Glow Paradise launched the “Chic Taouk”, pricing it at around $13 — nearly double what an un-chic chicken sandwich typically goes for in Beirut. The pricy pun proved hard to swallow, with outraged critics accusing the restaurant of overcharging in a country where many households struggle to afford basic necessities. Yet while the debate raged on social media, customers kept buying. The Glow Paradise sold more than 20,000 Chic Taouk sandwiches in just 11 days, according to managing partner Hrag Jeghalian, who described the online exchanges as "natural marketing". The contrasting reactions touched a nerve in Lebanon, where years of financial turmoil, political dysfunction and conflict have reshaped the country's social landscape, hollowing out much of the middle class while leaving a smaller group of consumers able to sustain an affluent lifestyle. DEBATE PULLS FOCUS AWAY FROM URGENT CRISES Sami Nader, an economist at the Saint Joseph University of Beirut, said the throngs at The Glow Paradise belied another reality. “So you see people in the restaurant, but what you don't see is that 22 restaurants closed last month,” Nader told Reuters. Lebanon’s Instagram-active community was split between those accusing the restaurant of theft and others saying the sandwich was intended for those who could afford it. Some questioned whether the dispute itself reflected misplaced priorities in a country grappling with urgent crises, from Israel’s[USN:L6N45P03S TEXT:" occupation"] of large swaths of the country’s south to the endemic electricity and water crises. Lebanon’s 2019 financial collapse was prompted by decades of corruption and profligate spending by the ruling elite, and several rounds of conflict since then have worsened the country’s economic outlook. GDP has declined by nearly 40% since 2019 and inflation is expected to rise to 17.5% due to rising global energy and shipping prices eating away at people’s purchasing power, according to the World Bank. The figure is more than quadruple the [USN:L1N43A0MP TEXT:"global headline inflation"] rate flagged by the International Monetary Fund in July. Four in five households in Lebanon struggle to afford basic necessities, the UN children’s agency said in September. 'PEOPLE CAN'T KEEP UP' The country’s middle class has “disappeared,” Nader said, dismantled by a series of crises including the collapse of the financial system in 2019, the 2020 Beirut Port explosion and two wars in under two years. Monthly bills from private generator operators, which provide electricity to many homes and businesses during outages on Lebanon's failing national grid, jumped by nearly 20% in August 2026 alone, bringing rates nearly 60% higher than they were in February of this year, according to the kilowatt-hour prices set by Lebanon’s energy ministry. For many, that means paying for 24/7 electricity now costs several hundred dollars a month, in a country where the minimum wage is set at $400. “Everything has become expensive, and people can’t keep up,” said Fouad Fakhreddine, a 53-year-old restaurant worker from nearby Hamra. “We are now getting paid, then getting in debt over that just to get by.” The years of economic instability, he said, have produced “a class that is living, and a class that is not dead and waiting to die from the unbearable situation it is in.” (This story has been refiled to change the name in the byline to Emilie Madi from Ahmad Al Kerdi.)

item.title: Four ways US foreign policy could change if Democrats win in November
item.description: Nonpartisan analysts say Democrats stand a good chance of winning the US House of Representatives and possibly the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, which would give them a slice of power in Washington after two years of Republican control.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: Nonpartisan analysts say Democrats stand a good chance of winning the US House of Representatives and possibly the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections , which would give them a slice of power in Washington after two years of Republican control. Democrats argue that Republicans have allowed President Donald Trump 's administration to declare war and control spending, even though the US Constitution reserves those powers for lawmakers. Here are some ways a Democratic Congress could hem in Trump's foreign policy. CURB THE IRAN WAR Trump did not secure approval from Congress before he launched the war with Iran on February 28, and Democrats have voted repeatedly to end the fighting unless he does so. One of these [USN:L1N42H0RZ TEXT:"resolutions passed"] with support from a handful of Republicans, but Trump's administration ignored it. With control of the House or the Senate, Democrats could cut defense spending to pressure Trump to obtain permission from Congress to continue the war. They could also require administration officials to testify publicly about their plans. FRESH SUPPORT FOR UKRAINE Trump has largely halted direct US financial and military aid to Ukraine, despite broad support from Democratic and Republican lawmakers as it fights a Russian invasion . Most recently, he has angered members of Congress, including many Republicans, by [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"lifting sanctions on Russian diesel"] and waiving sanctions on Russian energy only weeks after signing them into law. With a victory in both chambers in November, Democrats would be able to decide what gets voted on and when. That could allow them to approve new aid to Ukraine, which likely would pass with the two-thirds majorities needed to overcome a Trump veto. They could also target other Trump activities. For example, Representative Gregory Meeks of New York, who could head the House Foreign Affairs Committee if Democrats win control, has introduced bipartisan legislation to block Trump's plan to bring Russian diesel back into the global market. END MILITARY AID TO ISRAEL Support for Israel has plummeted among Democrats over its conduct in the Gaza war , which has killed tens of thousands of Palestinian civilians. The ongoing violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's close alliance with Republicans have also been factors. Democrats could limit or end military aid to Israel, which amounted to $3.8 billion in the most recent fiscal year. That is more than was provided to any other country. Nearly half of House Democrats voted this summer to cut off aid to Israel. Some of those who voted against that effort, such as Meeks, have backed limits on providing weapons like heavy bombs to Israel. LIMIT MILITARY SPENDING AND RESTORE FOREIGN AID Democrats are far more likely than Trump's Republicans to limit military spending. Trump asked for an unprecedented 67% increase in the military budget this year, to $1.5 trillion, but Democrats blocked it in the Senate, citing his refusal to consult Congress about the Iran war and his steep cuts to social programs. Trump has also withheld or canceled billions of dollars in foreign aid approved by Congress. Many Democrats have been angered by the cuts and say they will try to restore funding.

item.title: Trump campaigns in Michigan a day after Obama rallies Democrats
item.description: US President Donald Trump will rally Republicans in eastern Michigan on Sunday, a day after former President Barack Obama campaigned for Democrats in the state, underscoring its importance in next week's midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump will rally Republicans in eastern Michigan on Sunday, a day after former President Barack Obama campaigned for Democrats in the state, underscoring its importance in next week's midterm elections. Michigan has one of the nation's most competitive US Senate contests, an open-seat race between former Republican Representative Mike Rogers and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed that will help decide control of the chamber. Despite repeatedly attacking El-Sayed from the Oval Office and at rallies across the country, the Republican president had not yet campaigned in Michigan this year. If he wins, El-Sayed would be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Trump has sought to paint El-Sayed as a Muslim extremist and repeatedly [USN:L1N4620ZA TEXT:"mocked his middle name,"] Mohamed, a common Muslim name. El-Sayed has dismissed the accusation and, in a recent advertisement, defended his religion, saying, "faith is a thing there’s just too little of in Washington". Rogers has alleged without evidence that El-Sayed has [USN:L6N4661FE TEXT:"ties to the Muslim Brotherhood"], one of the Arab world's oldest and most influential Islamist groups. "If you are going to go to the United States Senate, we need to know: Are you for America or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?" Rogers said at a debate last week. El-Sayed has denied affiliation with the group and says it is "shameful" for Rogers to question his allegiance to the United States. At Saturday's rally in Detroit, Obama framed the attacks on El-Sayed as an attempt by opponents to make him look "less patriotic and less American than they are." The former president compared it to his experience as the target of [USN:KBN23O2P2 TEXT:"false claims"] that he was born in Kenya. "We have seen this movie before," Obama said. "I starred in it ... This stuff didn't work on me. Not in Michigan. It's not going to work on Abdul." Hours after the Detroit event, Trump dismissed Obama's efforts on behalf of El-Sayed. "Now he’s campaigning for a Muslim Brotherhood Jihadist, who hates Jews and Blacks and AMERICANS and TRUMP, and he is going to lose, also", Trump wrote in an early Sunday morning post on Truth Social. Trump's rally in Port Huron, part of an area of Michigan that he won in the 2024 presidential election with more than 66% of the vote, will also highlight the US-Canada tariff standoff. The trade fight has affected the Detroit-based [USN:L6N44N11O TEXT:"US auto industry,"] prompting Rogers to distance himself from the president's policy. Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the US Senate and US House of Representatives to overturn Republicans' narrow 53-47 and 218-214 majorities.

item.title: How Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy sites deepened the rift with Trump
item.description: The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump's frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv's supporters fear could threaten vital US support.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: Relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy took a sharp downward turn in recent weeks, with each leader openly criticizing the other. The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump's frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv's supporters fear could threaten vital US support going forward. Here's how the relationship soured: WHAT IS THE HISTORY OF TRUMP-ZELENSKIY TENSIONS? Trump has been skeptical of US involvement in Ukraine ever since his first term when, shortly after taking office in early 2017, he was asked to provide lethal aid to Ukraine and approved the sale of Javelin missiles to Kyiv. “Everyone around him wanted him to do it, and they pushed him hard and he eventually signed off on selling them Javelins, very reluctantly,” said a former senior Trump administration official, who spoke on condition of anonymity. “He didn’t consider it a core US interest. It was a European issue.” Trump's first major encounter with Zelenskiy came in a July 2019 phone call in which the Republican president asked the Ukrainian leader to investigate his Democratic rival Joe Biden and his son Hunter, in exchange for military support Congress had authorized. That episode led to Trump's first impeachment. Biden beat Trump in the 2020 presidential election. Trump also has fostered a relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin that runs against the norms of US foreign policy but echoes his warm ties with authoritarian leaders Xi Jinping of China and North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un. “Trump has always wanted better relations with Russia,” the former official said. WHAT DEEPENED THE RIFT BETWEEN THE TWO LEADERS? Trump's current frustration centers on Kyiv's [USN:S8N41C0VK TEXT:"attacks on Russian diesel infrastructure"]. Diesel prices have hit record highs since the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February, and global energy costs spiked. US lawmakers in Trump's Republican party face voter anger over inflation ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. On September 13, Trump began publicly calling on Ukraine to stop targeting diesel infrastructure. The following week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was also concerned that Ukraine had hit US-linked oil shipments. Ukraine has refused to halt the strikes, saying its long-range drone campaign is its only viable response to nearly five years of Russian bombardment. Moscow was forced in July to ban diesel exports as part of a raft of measures to address domestic fuel shortages. Angered by Zelenskiy’s defiance, Trump on October 9 announced a deal to buy diesel from Moscow, issuing a temporary general license that allows Russian diesel to reach the global market. He also waived sanctions on Russia authorized by a bill he signed into law in September. Suriya Jayanti, a former US official who runs a power sector company in Ukraine, said Russia’s strikes on Ukraine’s power grid have increased, despite Trump unilaterally announcing an [USN:FWN45X008 TEXT:"energy ceasefire"] on October 11. "It is clear to everyone in Kyiv that the goal is not actually an energy ceasefire, but it is really just an effort to hobble Ukraine and give Russia a decisive advantage," said Jayanti, who is also a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council think tank. HAS THE US THREATENED TO CUT OFF SUPPORT TO UKRAINE? Zelenskiy has said Ukrainian military officials had been threatened by US counterparts, who said continuing the energy strikes would lead the US to cut off intelligence sharing. A US official familiar with the situation disputed Kyiv's account. Speaking on condition of anonymity, the US official said there has been no increase in pressure on Ukraine. “We don't have to pressure Zelenskiy. If he wants to make a deal he'll make a deal. I think Putin is putting a ton of pressure on him and he (Zelenskiy) is putting some pressure on Russia but Russia doesn't seem to be minding it as much even though they are getting hit." On Thursday, Trump said he had asked SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to restore Ukraine’s access to the company's Starlink satellite system. Starlink's disruption temporarily hampered Kyiv's military drone operations and spurred fears that Kyiv would be left defenseless against Russia's attacks going into the winter. WHAT IS THE STATUS OF MOSCOW-KYIV PEACE TALKS? Peace efforts have continued but so far have not yielded tangible results. At talks in Oslo on October 20, Ukraine presented new proposals, and Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner repeated Trump's demand that Ukraine stop attacking Russian diesel refineries. The next day, envoy Witkoff – a close friend of Trump's - met Putin in St. Petersburg. Putin agreed to release detained American Stephen Hubbard in what the two countries called a goodwill gesture. Zelenskiy said on Friday that negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US would meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, a possible precursor to a meeting of the three countries’ leaders. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February.

item.title: Le suspect de l'attaque dans les Yvelines placé en observation psychiatrique
item.description: Le suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et cinq blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été placé en observation psychiatrique, le temps d'apprécier si son état de santé est compatible avec la poursuite des auditions, a annoncé dimanche le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et cinq blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été placé en observation psychiatrique, le temps d'apprécier si son état de santé est compatible avec la poursuite des auditions, a annoncé dimanche le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT). Ce placement en observation psychiatrique peut durer 48 heures et la garde à vue du suspect est suspendue durant cette période, a précisé le PNAT. Une analyse toxicologique a en outre permis de révéler la présence de cannabis et de cocaïne dans le sang de cet homme, a ajouté le PNAT. Les gardes à vue des membres de son entourage familial et amical se poursuivent. A la suite de cette attaque contre des passants commise à l'aide d'une arme automatique, le PNAT a ouvert une enquête du chef de "tentatives d'assassinats en relation avec une entreprise terroriste, avec la circonstance que les faits ont été commis à raison de l’appartenance vraie ou supposée, à une prétendue race, une ethnie, une nation ou une religion déterminée". Le président de la République Emmanuel Macron a qualifié cette attaque d'"attentat terroriste" à "caractère raciste avéré".

item.title: Jordan church attack survivor says her cousin died before her eyes
item.description: When gunmen opened fire on a church in Jordan, Sahar al-Halsa hid behind a pillar as she heard the shooting and people screaming in panic during a funeral service for her cousin's daughter.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi
item.content:encoded: When gunmen opened fire on a church in Jordan, Sahar al-Halsa hid behind a pillar as she heard the shooting and people screaming in panic during a funeral service for her cousin's daughter. When she rushed outside in the chaos, she said she spotted the assailants and another cousin lying on the ground wounded. "I went to him and said: 'Assem, Assem, my darling, answer me'," she said. She said he opened his eyes to look at her, but then "he was gone". Friday's attack on the Greek Orthodox place of worship in Karak governorate, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital Amman, prompted King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against Islamist militant groups, to order security forces to respond with an "iron fist" to what authorities described as extremist terrorism. PRIEST SENDS MESSAGE OF LOVE AND PEACE Nine people died in the shooting that witnesses said lasted for several minutes. The funeral services were held on Sunday. Eight of the victims’ coffins were wrapped in Jordanian flags before they were buried in a graveyard in the village of Hamoud, where the attack took place. Mourners and priests gathered at the scene. Forty people were wounded in the rare attack on minority Christians. Speaking from her home, from where the red dome of St George's church is visible, al-Halsa concluded that God must have saved her. "My life starts now, because I was going to die," she said, speaking beside her husband Ziad al-Halsa. A statue of Jesus on a cross was displayed on a shelf. Authorities have said they are still searching for the attackers, adding it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. There has been no immediate claim of responsibility. Ziad said he ran the short distance to the church after he heard the gunfire, describing the overwhelming sense of relief when he realised Sahar, who he described as "the love of his life", was safe. "To my cousins, may God have mercy on them," he said. Such attacks are highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though authorities there say they have foiled several Islamist plots in recent years. Speaking ahead of the funerals, priest Yuhanna Hamati said: "Our message from this church, from this place where this horrific crime was committed, is a message of love, peace, and reassurance. A message that we send to the whole world."

item.title: Employees group warns of major Swiss job losses if UBS relocates
item.description: As many as 12,000 UBS jobs in Switzerland could be at risk if tougher capital rules prompt the bank to relocate, according to the Swiss Bank Employees Association, or SBPV.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As many as 12,000 UBS (UBSG.S) jobs in Switzerland could be at risk if tougher capital rules prompt the bank to relocate, according to the Swiss Bank Employees Association, or SBPV. In a letter to lawmakers first published at the weekend by newspaper NZZ am Sonntag, the association warned that a relocation, sale or merger of UBS could cost 10,000 to 12,000 of UBS's roughly 34,000 jobs in Switzerland. The letter, which was also seen by Reuters, described this as the "worst case" scenario, and comes on top of cuts already made at the bank as it completes it integration of fallen rival Credit Suisse, which it acquired in 2023. UBS, which has repeatedly said it wants to remain in Switzerland, declined to comment on the SBPV estimate. A UBS spokesperson said the bank would keep job cuts resulting from the Credit Suisse takeover as low as possible. UBS said it still expects around 3,000 layoffs in Switzerland under the integration and that these would occur over several years, largely via steps like natural turnover, early retirements and insourcing of jobs once held externally. The SBPV warning comes as a committee in the lower house of the Swiss parliament [USN:L1N45N0NB TEXT:"prepares"] to discuss how much capital UBS should have to hold to back its foreign subsidiaries. Last month, the upper house [USN:L8N45F0DE TEXT:"proposed"] UBS should back those units with 90% Common Equity Tier 1 capital. UBS suggested that is [USN:L1N45C05I TEXT:"too much"] and the bank's chairman has warned it would need to carefully [USN:L8N4590WE TEXT:"consider"] its future in Switzerland if the rules are too harsh. Some shareholders of the bank have called for UBS to [USN:L1N45N061 TEXT:"leave"] Switzerland, and the bank has been [USN:L1N46205Q TEXT:"drafting"] potential contingency plans including shifting its headquarters or merging with another lender, sources have told Reuters. The SBPV letter, which also said UBS had a duty to commit to its Swiss base, urged lawmakers to pursue a "viable compromise" that did not impose such a heavy burden on the bank.

item.title: Clinical Catlin triumphs in Hong Kong Open
item.description: American John Catlin showed nerves of steel as he held local favourite Matthew Cheung and Finnish opponent Kalle Samooja at bay to win the Hong Kong Open, hitting seven birdies in Sunday's final round to finish five strokes ahead of his nearest challengers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: American John Catlin showed nerves of steel as he held local favourite Matthew Cheung and Finnish opponent Kalle Samooja at bay to win the Hong Kong Open, hitting seven birdies in Sunday's final round to finish five strokes ahead of his nearest challengers. Catlin, who won the Asian Tour Order of Merit in 2024, hit a six-under 64 in the fourth round to finish 20-under, earning his seventh title on the tour. Samooja led Cheung by a stroke going into the tricky 18th hole, but hit a bogey and had to settle for a joint second-place finish, as the latter secured the best finish for a Hong Kong player at the tournament in Fanling. "It's very, very special. Any time you can be on a trophy with some of the greatest players that ever played the game, I just feel very humble and very grateful," said Catlin. The 35-year-old was jointly leading the scoreboard along with Thomas Pieters and Caleb Surratt after the third round, where Cheung slipped from the top with three bogeys on Saturday. A clinical Catlin shook off a bogey on the fifth hole to take a solo lead on Sunday, and quickly fixed a mistake on the 14th as he found the centre of the green with a precise 120-yard stroke from thick grass to stay on course for a birdie. Error-prone Pieters and Surratt finished tied for sixth place with Sampson Zheng. Catlin's first trophy on the Asian Tour since April 2024 also earned him an invitation to next year's Open Championship and a maiden qualification for the Masters. "It's like a dream come true... it's been a long time coming, lot of hard work, lot of times when you weren't sure what was coming but you just kind of held the faith and I just kept working," Catlin said, shaking his head. "To finally be at the Masters, speechless."

item.title: NHL roundup: Leafs erupt in third, rout Oilers for fourth straight win
item.description: William Nylander scored two of Toronto's four third-period goals as the visiting Maple Leafs extended their winning streak to four with a 7-2 drubbing of the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: William Nylander scored two of Toronto's four third-period goals as the visiting Maple Leafs extended their winning streak to four with a 7-2 drubbing of the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday. Jack Roslovic recorded a goal and an assist, while Auston Matthews, Troy Stecher, Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri also scored and Kirill Marchenko nabbed two assists. For Edmonton, Leon Draisaitl scored twice and Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard had two helpers each. Anthony Stolarz stopped 30 shots for his fourth victory as Toronto posted its first four-game win streak since January. Tristan Jarry turned away 25 shots for the Oilers, who had won three in a row. With his 11th and 12th goals of the season, Draisaitl shares the NHL lead with the Minnesota Wild's Kirill Kaprizov. Draisaitl is second in the league in scoring with 23 points -- 10 shy of McDavid, who has eight goals and a league-leading 25 assists. Mammoth 5, Lightning 4 (OT) Dmitri Simashev scored his first NHL goal and also netted the game-winning tally in overtime, lifting Utah past Tampa Bay in Salt Lake City. Simashev slipped in a pass from Barrett Hayton at 1:44 for his first career game-winner. Utah also received goals from Kailer Yamamoto, Dylan Guenther and Anders Lee. Vincent Trocheck had two assists. Mammoth goaltender Karel Vejmelka made 29 saves and earned the secondary assist on Simashev's winner. Jake Guentzel, Pontus Holmberg, Brayden Point and Conor Geekie hit the net for the Lightning, and Dennis Hildeby made 23 saves. Nikita Kucherov collected an assist for his 1,138th career point, passing Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead. Blue Jackets 2, Golden Knights 1 (OT) Adam Fantilli scored a power-play goal 59 seconds into overtime to lead Columbus to a victory over visiting Vegas. It was Fantilli's third goal of the season and snapped a 0-for-22 drought on the power play for the Blue Jackets. Denton Mateychuk also scored a goal, Kent Johnson added two assists and Cam Talbot finished with 26 saves. Tomas Hertl scored for Vegas and Hart stopped 18 of 20 shots for Vegas, which saw its losing streak extended to a season-high three games. The Golden Knights have allowed a power-play goal in five straight games. Penguins 3, Predators 2 (OT) Ville Koivunen scored with 1:16 left in overtime for ailing Pittsburgh, which rallied to take down visiting Nashville. Connor Dewar and Rickard Rakell also scored for the Penguins, who won their second straight game. Arturs Silovs finished with 24 saves, marking the first time the team has won consecutive games since starting the season 2-0. Steven Stamkos scored his fifth of the season and Jayden Struble notched his first for the Predators, who are 0-4 in overtime and shootouts. Juuse Saros made a season-high 34 saves, but Rakell spoiled his bid for a victory by tying the game with 1:06 remaining in regulation. Bruins 6, Sharks 4 Boston scored four third-period goals, including three in a row to erase a 3-2 deficit, to edge visiting San Jose and run its unbeaten streak to eight games. David Pastrnak tied former teammate Patrice Bergeron for third on Boston's all-time goals list (427) to kick off the late-game surge. Fraser Minten (game-winner), James Hagens and Casey Mittelstadt all had a goal and an assist, while Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka each dished out two assists, and Jeremy Swayman made 23 saves. Michael Misa, Kiefer Sherwood, Dmitry Orlov and Will Smith each scored a goal, Jacob Trouba had two assists, and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 29 shots for the Sharks, who were on a two-game win streak. Ducks 5, Flyers 4 Tristan Luneau had a goal and two assists as visiting Anaheim snapped a five-game losing streak with a victory over Philadelphia. Leo Carlsson chipped in with a goal and an assist against the team that signed him to a five-year, $90 million offer sheet over the summer. Anaheim ultimately matched the deal, making the 21-year-old the highest paid player in the league. Beckett Sennecke and A.J. Greer also scored and Lukas Dostal turned aside 28 shots. Matvei Michkov scored his seventh and eighth goals for Philadelphia, which had won three straight since losing its first nine. Porter Martone had a goal and an assist and Tyson Foerster also scored, while Trevor Zegras recorded two assists against his former team. Joseph Woll finished with 21 saves. Devils 3, Kings 1 Arseny Gritsyuk scored for the fifth straight game to help New Jersey seal a win against Los Angeles in Newark, N.J. Anthony Mantha and Brett Pesce also scored, and Jake Allen made 12 saves for New Jersey, which has won three straight and five of the past six. Scott Laughton scored and Anton Forsberg made 23 saves for the Kings, who had won two in a row following a 0-4-2 start to the season. Senators 7, Rangers 4 Drake Batherson scored a hat trick and added an assist as Ottawa topped visiting New York. Jake Sanderson tallied one goal and added two assists, while Dylan Cozens and Michael Amadio each scored and chipped in a helper. Tim Stutzle also found the back of the net as Ottawa improved to 5-2-0 on home ice. Jonas Johansson, making his Senators and season debut, made 24 saves. J.T. Miller and Will Cuylle each scored and added an assist, and Alexis Lafreniere and Pavel Dorofeyev also scored for the Rangers, who are 1-3-1 in their last five. Adam Fox and Noah Laba each added a pair of helpers, and Dylan Garand stopped 17 shots. Hurricanes 4, Blues 0 Pyotr Kochetkov made 24 saves to lead Carolina to a road victory over St. Louis. Sean Walker, Jesperi Kotkaniemi, Logan Stankoven, and Nikolaj Ehlers all lit the lamp as the Hurricanes closed out their five-game road trip with a victory and a 3-2-0 record. Sebastian Aho and Seth Jarvis each picked up a pair of assists, while Joel Hofer finished with 35 saves in the losing effort. Wild 5, Kraken 1 Kirill Kaprizov scored his 12th goal of the season -- tying for the league lead -- and added an assist as Minnesota dominated host Seattle. Kaprizov, who is tied for first in goals with the Edmonton Oilers' Leon Draisaitl, opened the scoring on a breakaway just 26 seconds into the game. Blake Coleman scored twice, including an empty-netter with 3:36 remaining, while Joel Eriksson Ek added a goal and an assist and Olli Maatta also tallied. Jesper Wallstedt made 23 saves. Berkly Catton scored for the Kraken, who had won their previous two games. Joey Daccord stopped 31 of 35 shots. Capitals 4, Sabres 3 Alex Tuch scored his second goal of the game at 3:42 of overtime to lift host Washington to victory over Buffalo, his former team. Tuch, acquired by Washington in a sign-and-trade deal with Buffalo in June, was in the slot to take a pass from Dylan Strome behind the net and beat a screened Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen inside the left post. Strome also scored twice, and Charlie Lindgren made 18 saves for the Capitals. Jack Quinn, Josh Doan and Noah Ostlund scored for the Sabres, who built a 2-0 lead halfway through the first period. Luukkonen made 30 saves. Flames 4, Red Wings 1 Joel Farabee scored a goal and added two assists as Calgary cruised past visiting Detroit, snapping the Red Wings' eight-game winning streak in the series. Matvei Gridin had a goal and an assist for the Flames, while Ryan Strome and Zayne Parekh also scored. Matt Coronato added two assists. Devin Cooley made 28 saves for Calgary, which has won three straight and four of their last five games after opening the season with five consecutive losses. Andrew Copp scored the lone goal for Detroit, which had won three of its previous four games. John Gibson made 21 saves after leaving his previous start Thursday because of an eye issue. --Field Level Media

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Russian Defence Ministry said on Sunday that its drones had struck a cargo vessel bound for the Black Sea port of Chornomorsk during an overnight attack. The ministry said the vessel was being used to supply the Ukrainian army. Russian forces also hit a logistics centre, a distribution centre and a logistics terminal in the Ukrainian city of Kharkiv. The ministry said the facilities had been used for storage and distribution of dual-use cargo for the Ukrainian military. Reuters could not independently verify the Defence Ministry's information.

item.title: NBA roundup: Nikola Jokic records 199th triple-double, Nuggets top Pels
item.description: Nikola Jokic recorded 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, Jamal Murray poured in 42 points and the Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to top the visiting New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nikola Jokic recorded 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, Jamal Murray poured in 42 points and the Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to top the visiting New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night. Jokic has 199 career regular-season triple-doubles in 12 seasons, second to just-retired Russell Westbrook's 209 in 18 seasons starting in 2008-09. Trevon Brazile scored seven of his 17 points in overtime and hit a corner 3-pointer late in the extra period, Christian Braun had 15 points in the game and DeMar DeRozan added 12 points for the Nuggets. Trey Murphy III led the Pelicans with 26 points, Dejounte Murray had 22, Zion Williamson and Derik Queen contributed 17 each, Saddiq Bey scored 14 and Jeremiah Fears added 10. Hornets 115, Heat 110 Brandon Miller pumped in 34 points and Charlotte recovered from blowing a 23-point lead to beat visiting Miami. Dennis Schroder added 25 points, Naz Reid scored 23 and Grayson Allen contributed 20. Miller was the only one of the Hornets' top four scorers who played for the team last season. Davion Mitchell's 22 points and 10 assists paced the Heat, who remained winless through three games despite erasing a 23-point deficit to tie the score at 100. Bam Adebayo's 20 points and eight rebounds gave Miami a lift, Pelle Larsson supplied 15 points, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson each had 14, and Bobby Portis scored 13. Cavaliers 125, Nets 121 Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points and Jarrett Allen had 21 points and eight rebounds as Cleveland built a 22-point lead before holding on for a victory over visiting Brooklyn. Evan Mobley added 20 points and 10 rebounds, and Jaylon Tyson scored 15 points off the bench in the Cavaliers' home opener. James Harden collected 12 points, eight rebounds and seven assists as Cleveland picked up its first win. Brooklyn, which trailed 104-82 with 9:29 remaining, pulled within 123-121 on Michael Porter Jr.'s 3-pointer with 8.1 seconds left. Porter (28 points, nine rebounds) fouled out on the subsequent possession and Sam Merrill hit two free throws to put the Cavaliers up four with 5.2 seconds remaining. Julius Randle had 23 points for winless Brooklyn. 76ers 127, Bucks 116 Joel Embiid recorded his 10th career triple-double and Jaylen Brown scored 27 points on his 30th birthday to lead Philadelphia to a home win over Milwaukee. Embiid finished with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for the 76ers, who rested LeBron James (back/sciatica). James is expected to play Sunday against the Detroit Pistons, while Embiid will rest in the second half of a back-to-back. Tyrese Maxey pitched in with 26 points, while VJ Edgecombe delivered a 17-point, 13-rebound effort. While Philadelphia is 3-0 on the young season, the Bucks fell to 0-3 despite eight players scoring in double figures. Jaime Jaquez Jr. led Milwaukee with 21 points, while Kel'el Ware had 19 points and 13 rebounds off the bench for the visitors. Wizards 124, Bulls 120 Trae Young paired 25 points with nine assists and Kyshawn George added 22 points and nine rebounds as Washington downed host Chicago to open a three-game road trip. The Wizards outscored the Bulls 40-20 in the third quarter. Anthony Davis and Young combined to go 6-for-6 from the free-throw line to hold onto the lead. Davis (19 points) and Tre Johnson (13) also scored in double figures for Washington, while Justin Champagnie had an 11-point, 14-rebound double-double. Chicago rookie Caleb Wilson contributed 30 points and 14 rebounds for his first career double-double, and teammate Matas Buzelis scored 21 points. Norman Powell added 18, Jalen Smith had 14 and Tre Jones 10. Josh Giddey had nine points, 10 assists and eight rebounds. Miles Bridges scored 16 points and Dillon Brooks added 15 points for the Suns, who won their home opener. Booker set a franchise record for points in a home opener. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 26 points and nine rebounds and De'Anthony Melton scored 25 points for the Warriors, who fell to 0-3 for the first time since 2007-08. Golden State was without starters Stephen Curry (knee), Brandin Podziemski (back) and Draymond Green (back) and reserve Al Horford (back). Spurs 122, Mavericks 106 Victor Wembanyama scored 23 points as visiting San Antonio earned its first win of the season by defeating short-handed Dallas in the second of a back-to-back for both teams. Dylan Harper added 22 points, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle scored 19 each, Julian Champagnie hit for 12 off the bench and Devin Vassell tallied 11 points for the Spurs. Wembanyama also posted seven rebounds and four blocks. The Mavericks played without stars Cooper Flagg (shoulder) and Kyrie Irving, who was held out for left knee injury management. Flagg sprained his left shoulder in a win at Indiana on Friday and will be reevaluated next week. Rookie Sergio De Larrea's 21 points led Dallas. Marcus Sasser, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford scored 12 apiece. Rockets 121, Hawks 114 Kevin Durant led seven double-figure scorers with 22 points as Houston topped host Atlanta to improve to 3-0. The Rockets also got 19 points apiece from Tari Eason and Reed Sheppard, who started in place of Fred VanVleet (right knee load management). Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each scored 17 points, with Sengun grabbing 10 rebounds and Thompson collecting 11. The Hawks were led by Jalen Johnson, who fell just shy of a triple-double with 26 points, 16 assists and nine rebounds. item.title: Brazil votes in tight runoff between leftist Lula and Bolsonaro Jr.
item.description: Corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling dominated the race.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin
item.content:encoded: Brazilians voted on Sunday in a tight runoff vote that could shift Latin America's largest nation sharply rightward, bringing it closer to the United States as part of a broader conservative shift across the region. The runoff pits leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro. Flavio scored [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"a major upset at the start of the month"] by defying pollsters to lead voting in the first round. A victory for Bolsonaro, 45, would extend a wave of right-wing victories for Latin American candidates friendly to US President Donald Trump while a fourth mandate for Lula would be a disappointment in Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security. Reuters on Saturday [USN:L1N4650X8 TEXT:"revealed a campaign"] within Trump's State Department to help get the Bolsonaros back in power. Brazil's election race has been dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling, which Washington denies. It has also been colored by fallout from [USN:L1N43T0Q4 TEXT:"Jair Bolsonaro's 2025"] conviction for plotting a 2022 coup, with Flavio pledging to free his father if elected. Trump has called the case a "witch hunt" and imposed a 50% tariff on Brazil in 2025, in a decision explicitly linked to Jair Bolsonaro’s trial. While this was later watered down, Trump unleashed [USN:L1N43P1HE TEXT:"new levies against Brazil this year"], citing unfair trade practices. Lula has cast the Trump administration’s proximity to the Bolsonaro clan as part of an attempt to sway the election, while labeling tariffs and other punitive measures as bullying. On economic issues, despite falling inequality and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over an electorate grappling with high living costs and heavy household debt. Endemic gang violence also weighs on voters’ minds. Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns and has promised a heavy-handed approach to fighting crime, pledging maximum-security jails and chemical castration for serious sexual offenses. Casting his ballot in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday, Flavio Bolsonaro urged people to come out vote "come rain or shine". Lula, meanwhile, is due to vote in São Bernardo do Campo, near Sao Paulo. CANDIDATES ARE NECK AND NECK Polls show the candidates are practically tied going into the runoff. Historical precedent favors Bolsonaro, however, as no candidate has ever won the presidency after coming second in the first-round vote. Bolsonaro picked up 47% of ballots cast in the first round, while Lula trailed with 45%. The senator's first-round win [USN:L6N45Q08A TEXT:"sent Brazil's markets and currency soaring"] on expectations of pro-business reforms. His first-round success was mirrored in congressional elections for his Liberal Party and other right-wing politicians, which could pave a legislative path for him, or complicate governance for Lula.

item.title: Disenchanted Netanyahu supporters are prize of Israel election campaign
item.description: Labor has dwindled to a rump as Israeli politics have shifted rightwards, and there are now around half a dozen other parties courting Likud voters, from the center to the far right.
item.dc:creator: Emily Rose, Maayan Lubell
item.content:encoded: In the remote Negev Desert town of Dimona, long a bastion of Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party, disenchanted voters are going door-to-door campaigning for his top rival, hoping to bring down the veteran prime minister in Israel's election on Tuesday. The ballot is Israel's first since Hamas' October 7, 2023, surprise attack that shook the country and plunged the region into turmoil, as Israel went to war on the militant group in Gaza and its allies in Lebanon and Iran. The October 7 security breach saw Likud's popularity plummet. Opinion polls for months have predicted Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties losing its majority. But his top rival, centrist Gadi Eisenkot, has no clear path to power either, and the race has become tighter as the election nears. Dimona, where an Iranian missile wounded dozens in March, has become a political battleground. "We must have change. Bibi has to go," said Yossi Assayag, 74, who says he has supported Likud most his life. "Bibi has brought disaster to Israel." LIKUD LOYALISTS Assayag is part of a cohort of town residents trying to convince their community to vote for Eisenkot's party Yashar, which is neck-and-neck with Likud in the polls. It's a tough task in Dimona, where half the voters in the previous 2022 election cast a ballot for Likud. "I will never betray Likud," said Ruti Ohana, a pensioner, who says she has voted Likud ever since immigrating to Israel from North Africa more than 60 years ago. She said Netanyahu was a cut above his rivals, and the blame he receives from detractors for October 7 was unfair. Right-wing Likud long ago formed a core voter base among Jews of Middle Eastern and North African descent, known as Mizrahis, who felt neglected by the European-influenced centre-left Labor Party that dominated Israel for generations. Labor has since dwindled to a rump as Israeli politics have shifted rightwards, and there are now around half a dozen other parties courting Likud voters, from the centre to the far right. But the link to the party among its past supporters remains strong. "Most people here vote for Likud just because that's how they were raised," said Oria Asaf, 25, a past Likud voter now backing Yashar. "The change will come when people start to think about their children's future rather than their parents' past." BATTLE FOR WAVERING LIKUDNIKS While Netanyahu has a hard core of supporters that can't be won over, the prize is undecided voters who "understand that we are in a state of crisis" and are open to persuasion, said Michal Elmalem Abu, elected as a member of the city council from Likud and now leading Eisenkot's Dimona campaign. Some 13% of Israeli voters have yet to decide how they will vote, according to data collected by the Viterbi Family Center for Public Opinion and Policy Research at the Israel Democracy Institute. Of those who voted for Likud in 2022, just 55% now say they will vote for the party again on Tuesday. Fifteen percent will support parties aligned against Netanyahu, including 8% for Yashar. Another 14% will vote for alternative right-wing parties, and 9% are undecided. It is in places just like Dimona where Eisenkot stands a chance to bite a chunk out of Likud's base, said Amotz Asa-El, a political scientist at the Hartman Institute. A child of Moroccan immigrants who rose through the ranks to become military chief of staff, Eisenkot, 66, has a personal story of humble origins from the Mizrahi community that "appeals to a big swath of the Israeli electorate, particularly Likud's traditional electorate", said Asa-El. In an electoral field crowded with ex-soldiers, his peerless security credentials are an asset. The loss of his son, killed in combat in Gaza in December 2023, resonates with voters. At a town hall during a visit to Dimona in July, residents said they were excited about the prospect of a leader of Mizrahi descent. Others approached him with hugs and tearful condolences for the loss of his son. But a week later Netanyahu held his own event, demonstrating his powerful appeal in the hardscrabble Negev, where Likud governments have long boasted of bringing development funds. "Look around you, look at your community, look at what was here then and what is here now, and ask yourselves which governments invested in this monumental effort. And I do this out of immense love," he said. Lior Katzav, a Likud former mayor of Kiryat Malachi, another small-town stronghold, said party surveys show voters who had abandoned Likud are returning as the election nears. But even some who are sympathetic to Netanyahu say it may be time for a change. Israel's youngest prime minister when he was first elected 30 years ago, he has since become its longest-serving, now 77, having governed for 18 years over six terms. "It's time for him to go," said Dimona software engineer David Iskali. "He's done a lot for Israel but it can't go on. I won't give my vote to someone almost 80-years-old."

item.title: World Series rematch, Indian edition: Yankees beat Dodgers in Mumbai event
item.description: Mumbai's cricket fans packed the stands at the Andheri Sports Complex on Saturday to watch Indian World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav swing a bat - just not the kind that they are used to.
item.dc:creator: Revathi Hariharan
item.content:encoded: Mumbai's cricket fans packed the stands at the Andheri Sports Complex on Saturday to watch Indian World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav swing a bat - just not the kind that they are used to. Indian cricketers Suryakumar Yadav, Shardul Thakur, Deepak Chahar and Radha Yadav lined up alongside ex-Major League Baseball players Nick Swisher, Adrian Gonzalez, Jake Arrieta and Jonny Gomes in a three-on-three tournament that organisers pitched as a bridge between the two bat-and-ball games. Each of the four teams mixed a baseball veteran, an Indian cricketer and an American softball player and the scoring rewarded both muscle and precision. A home run earned two points, hitting the target zone earned four and fielders picked up one point for a catch, while five consecutive out-of-the-park hits doubled a team's total. The semifinals offered up both a thriller and a stroll, as Gonzalez's Los Angeles Dodgers overturned the Shardul-led Chicago Cubs' 44 runs with just a minute to spare, while Suryakumar's New York Yankees cruised past the Boston Red Sox. That set up a rematch of the 2024 World Series, this time in India, with the Yankees posting 78 and holding off the Dodgers to be crowned champions. Softball player Rachel Garcia was named the tournament's most valuable player. Suryakumar, a former India captain who guided the side to victory at this year's Twenty20 Cricket World Cup on home soil, said he is confident baseball will grow in India and that cricketing skills can translate to success in the American sport. "I think it's all about good range hitting," added Suryakumar, whose celebrations spilled into the stands as he placed the gold chain he won around his wife's neck after the win. "You must be strong from head to your lower body, have a good core and strong arms. If you want to hit 450 feet, 500 feet, you got to be strong. Work hard. No substitutes."

item.title: Borr Drilling rig sinks off Gabon, one person dead and four missing
item.description: Borr Drilling's Prospector 5 drilling rig sank late on Saturday off the coast of Mayumba, Gabon, killing one worker and leaving four others missing among the 115 people on board, officials and the company said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Gnaneshwar Rajan, Colleen Goko
item.content:encoded: Borr Drilling's (BORR.N) Prospector 5 drilling rig sank late on Saturday off the coast of Mayumba, Gabon, killing one worker and leaving four others missing among the 115 people on board, officials and the company said on Sunday. One of the five initially unaccounted for, an Indian national, has been found dead, according to Sylvain Mayabi Binet, secretary general of the National Organization of Petroleum Employees. The remaining four missing people are three Gabonese nationals and one other expatriate. "Preliminary information indicates that the rig experienced a punch-through event during preload activities, resulting in loss of stability and the subsequent sinking of the rig," the offshore drilling contractor said. The Prospector 5 oil and gas rig, owned and operated by Borr, is contracted to support BW Energy's (BWE.OL) drilling operations off Gabon. The rig had not yet begun drilling. Prospector 5 is located at the Dussafu Marin permit, a licence off the Gabon coast. BW Energy holds a 73.5% working interest in the licence, with Panoro Energy holding 17.5%. Gabon's Ministry of Petroleum and Gas said it had activated a crisis unit and ordered the navy to reinforce search and rescue operations at sea. The ministry also ordered a technical investigation, Petroleum and Gas Minister Clotaire Kondja said in a statement. The crisis unit brings together the ministry, the navy, state oil company Gabon Oil, BW Energy and Borr Drilling, Kondja said. The accident occurred at approximately 9:40 p.m. (2040 GMT) on Saturday in the Dussafu Marin permit area near the Mabomont production facility, the ministry said. "We are deeply concerned for those who remain unaccounted for and everyone affected by this incident," said Borr Drilling Chief Executive Bruno Morand. "Our immediate priority is supporting the ongoing search and rescue efforts and the welfare of all personnel involved." Panoro Energy (PENR.OL) said production had been halted, adding that there were no reports of damage or accidental discharges. No discharge of harmful substances has been observed, the ministry said, adding that pollution-response resources remained deployed to protect the coastline and nearby Mayumba National Park.

item.title: Guadalajara gana de visita en el torneo mexicano de fútbol
item.description: Guadalajara, el club más popular del fútbol mexicano, ganó el sábado 1-0 de visita a Monterrey en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Guadalajara, el club más popular del fútbol mexicano, ganó el sábado 1-0 de visita a Monterrey en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura. Las "Chivas" de Guadalajara llegaron a 26 puntos para mantenerse en el segundo lugar general, por abajo del líder América que registra 27 unidades. En el partido, disputado en el estadio BBVA de Monterrey, Guadalajara anotó el gol del triunfo a los nueve minutos con un disparo cruzado de Roberto "Piojo" Alvarado tras recibir un pase de Santiago Sandoval, quien aprovechó un error defensivo de Víctor Guzmán para robar el balón. Monterrey tuvo la opción de empatar a los 19 minutos con un tiro penal, pero el portero Raúl Rangel atajó el disparo del argentino Lucas Ocampos. Los "Rayados" de Monterrey habían rescatado el empate en tiempo de reposición cuando el balón le rebotó en el pecho a Diego Rossi tras un desvío defensivo, pero el árbitro anuló el gol tras revisar en el VAR la jugada en la que el balón le pegó en la mano al centrocampista uruguayo. "Me gustó mucho el comportamiento del equipo en el aspecto defensivo y el orden que tuvimos para neutralizar a un equipo que cuenta con jugadores de mucho talento, con mucho desequilibrio y, además, muy bien trabajado. Me gustó el esfuerzo colectivo y la garra con la que se jugó el partido, es muy importante que mi equipo juegue con ese espíritu competitivo", dijo en conferencia de prensa el director técnico de Guadalajara, el argentino Gabriel Milito. "Siempre digo que la contundencia es fundamental en el fútbol, encontrar el gol es determinante, pero también es muy importante generar situaciones, peor sería no generarlas, porque si no creas oportunidades es imposible marcar goles. El camino que queda por delante es duro, primero tenemos que terminar el torneo y después vendrá la Liguilla (Postemporada)", agregó. A la postemporada o liguilla clasifican los clubes que ocupan los primeros ocho lugares de la tabla general al final de las 17 jornadas de la temporada regular. En los otros partidos disputados el sábado, Pumas UNAM y Tigres UANL empataron 1-1 con goles del paraguayo Robert Morales y del argentino Juan Francisco Brunetta, respectivamente. León y Toluca empataron 1-1. Para León anotó José Alvarado, mientras que para los "Diablos Rojos" de Toluca lo hizo el uruguayo Federico Viñas. La jornada finalizará el domingo cuando Atlas sea local ante Puebla, el actual campeón Cruz Azul visite a Querétaro, América juegue ante Pachuca y Tijuana sea rival de Santos Laguna. El viernes, Atlético de San Luis ganó de visita al Atlante por 1-0. Por su parte, Necaxa y Bravos de Ciudad Juárez empataron 1-1.

item.title: Kawano, Henderson set world marathon race walk records
item.description: Japan's Masatora Kawano and Australia's Rebecca Henderson set the men's and women's world records for the marathon race walks at the All Japan Race Walking meet in Takahata on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan's Masatora Kawano and Australia's Rebecca Henderson set the men's and women's world records for the marathon race walks at the All Japan Race Walking meet in Takahata on Sunday. Kawano, a two-time world championships medallist in the 35-km event, set the inaugural men’s world record for the distance, with a time of 2:55:14. Henderson improved on Italian [USN:L1N44C02R TEXT:"Sofia Fiorini's record"] from the European Athletics Championships, clocking 3:14:52 at the World Athletics Race Walking Tour Bronze event. The half marathon and marathon became official race walk distances in January this year.

item.title: Flames continue turnaround, top Wings for third straight win
item.description: Joel Farabee scored a goal and added two assists as the Calgary Flames cruised past the visiting Detroit Red Wings 4-1 on Saturday, snapping Detroit's eight-game winning streak in the teams' series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joel Farabee scored a goal and added two assists as the Calgary Flames cruised past the visiting Detroit Red Wings 4-1 on Saturday, snapping Detroit's eight-game winning streak in the teams' series. Matvei Gridin had a goal and an assist for Calgary, while Ryan Strome and Zayne Parekh also scored. Matt Coronato added two assists. Devin Cooley made 28 saves for the Flames, who have won three straight and four of their last five games after opening the season with five consecutive losses. Andrew Copp scored the lone goal for Detroit, which had won three of its previous four games. John Gibson made 21 saves after leaving his previous start Thursday because of an eye issue. Farabee, who extended his point streak to four games with two goals and four assists during that span, put Calgary on the board at 17:50 of the first period. Adam Klapka set him up for a snap shot, while Kevin Bahl also assisted on Farabee's second goal of the season. Copp tied the game at 2:22 of the second period with his second goal of the season. J.T. Compher set him up for a backhand shot past Cooley. Parekh put Calgary back in front at 8:38 with a power-play snap shot for his first goal of the season. Strome extended the lead to 3-1 at 17:04, converting a pass from Morgan Frost for his second goal of the season. Gridin capped the scoring at 18:30 of the second period with a power-play snap shot for his second goal of the campaign. The Flames will look to complete a sweep of their four-game homestand Monday against the Toronto Maple Leafs, while the Red Wings will try to split their four-game road trip Monday against the Edmonton Oilers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Australian Grand Prix called off as rain spoils Phillip Island send-off
item.description: The MotoGP race was delayed by two hours due to the weather, before organisers threw in the towel and finally called it off.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The final Australian MotoGP at the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit was called off on Sunday due to heavy rain, ruining the farewell for one of the championship's most beloved circuits. It was a crushing blow for the sold-out crowd [USN:L6N46607H TEXT:"at Phillip Island,"] with the Australian Grand Prix moving to the streets of Adelaide next year. The Moto2 and Moto3 races were cancelled first and the MotoGP race was delayed by two hours due to the weather, before organisers threw in the towel and finally called it off at 3:40 p.m. (0440 GMT). "Due to limited visibility affecting the operation of the medical helicopter the MotoGP Grand Prix race has been cancelled," MotoGP said in a statement. "The MotoGP riders will do a lap behind the safety car and stop on the main straight to greet the fans. Pitlane will open for the farewell lap at 15:45 local time." RIDER PARADE The dark clouds and pelting rain brought down the visibility around the circuit, affecting the medical helicopter, which would take 45 minutes to reach the circuit from mainland Melbourne in an emergency.
