Other than two years lost to the COVID-19 pandemic, the seaside track south of Melbourne had been a fixture on the world championship calendar for 30 years and produced some of Australian motorcycling's most memorable moments. Australian two-times world champion Casey Stoner celebrated six wins in succession from 2007 to 2012, while compatriot Mick Doohan sealed his fifth and final world title with victory in the 1998 race. The raincoat-clad fans who persevered through the rain were treated to a farewell lap from the MotoGP riders, who waved as they slowly made their way around a soaking wet track. Home racer Jack Miller did his best to entertain his supporters with a series of tricks, including a stand-up wheelie over the finish line, before heading over to the grandstand and throwing his gloves and boots into the crowd. MILLER DEJECTED, SIGH OF RELIEF FOR MARTIN The Pramac Racing rider, a very strong performer in the wet, cut a dejected figure when he was interviewed after completing his lap. "This is a tough pill to swallow," said the 31-year-old, who will be leaving MotoGP at the end of the season after more than a decade to join Pata Maxus Yamaha in the World Superbike Championship. "You know, I was praying for rain all weekend. We got the rain, but obviously we weren't organised enough to get the racing going, so it's a tough one. "You guys deserve better. Honestly, all of you have done a fantastic job turning out for Phillip Island, sitting through traffic, sitting through dog-shit weather, all the rest of it. You guys are amazing. Thank you very much." Rain had been expected for the weekend, but MotoGP did not revive its 2023 strategy for the circuit, when the Grand Prix was moved ahead to Saturday and the sprint scheduled for Sunday. That sprint race three years ago was eventually called off. The cancellation of the race also ended the opportunity for seven-times MotoGP champion Marquez to extend his lead in the championship standings, with his title rival Martin declared unfit to compete in the race after [USN:L1N46A017 TEXT:"fracturing his wrist."] Martin held the championship lead heading into the weekend but finds himself 10 points behind Marquez after failing to finish Saturday's sprint after a gruesome crash. On Sunday, Martin's team Aprilia said he would not travel back to Spain to undergo treatment, however, boosting the 2024 champion's hopes of racing at next week's Malaysian Grand Prix and remaining in the title fight.

item.title: Devin Booker, Suns continue Warriors' rough start to season
item.description: Devin Booker had 43 points, seven assists and seven rebounds and the host Phoenix Suns beat Golden State 131-122 on Saturday to send the Warriors to their worst start in almost two decades.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Devin Booker had 43 points, seven assists and seven rebounds and the host Phoenix Suns beat Golden State 131-122 on Saturday to send the Warriors to their worst start in almost two decades. Miles Bridges scored 16 points and Dillon Brooks added 15 points for the Suns, who won their home opener after suffering a 41-point defeat at Portland in their season opener Wednesday. Booker set a franchise record for points in a home opener. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 26 points and nine rebounds and De'Anthony Melton scored 20 of his 25 points in the second half for the skeleton-crew Warriors, who fell to 0-3 for the first time since 2007-08, when they lost their first six before finishing 48-34. Golden State, playing the second of a back-to-back, was without starters Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski and Draymond Green and reserve Al Horford. Curry (knee), Podziemski (back) and Horford (back) were held out for injury management. Green missed with low back soreness. Brandon Williams added 20 points for the Warriors, who blew a 12-point lead in the final four minutes of a 111-108 home loss to Memphis on Friday. Lendeborg made six of the Warriors' 17 3-pointers on Saturday. Melton had four. Melton scored 13 points in the third quarter, when the Warriors used a 12-0 run to take a 73-71 lead before the Suns came back. Booker's four-point play with 35 seconds left in the third quarter made it 99-89 for Phoenix. Luke Kennard's 3-pointer pushed the Suns' lead to 117-102 with 6:07 remaining in the game. Kennard had 11 points and three 3-pointers in his Suns debut after missing the season opener with a knee injury. The Warriors made 17 of 39 3-pointers (43.6%) and turned 19 offensive rebounds into 26 points. The Suns knocked the Warriors out of the postseason a year ago with a 111-96 victory in the play-in round. Lendeborg had six points on a pair of threes and Graham Ike had six points and five rebounds in the first quarter, when the Warriors took an early seven-point lead and had a 25-22 edge at the quarter. Ike, a 6-foot-9 rookie, made his second straight start at center as the Warriors also played without Kristaps Porzingis, who is not with the team because of an undisclosed health issue. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kirill Kaprizov's early goal sets tone as Wild handle Kraken
item.description: Kirill Kaprizov scored his NHL-leading 12th goal of the season and added an assist as the Minnesota Wild defeated the host Seattle Kraken 5-1 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kirill Kaprizov scored his NHL-leading 12th goal of the season and added an assist as the Minnesota Wild defeated the host Seattle Kraken 5-1 on Saturday night. Blake Coleman scored twice, including an empty-netter with 3:36 remaining, while Joel Eriksson Ek added a goal and an assist and Olli Maatta also tallied for the Wild. Minnesota snapped a two-game losing streak and improved to 1-1-1 on its five-game trip, which concludes with stops Sunday at Vancouver and Tuesday at Utah. Goaltender Jesper Wallstedt made 23 saves. Berkly Catton scored for Seattle, which had won its previous two games. Joey Daccord stopped 31 of 35 shots. Kaprizov, who is tied for first in goals with the Edmonton Oilers' Leon Draisaitl, opened the scoring on a breakaway just 26 seconds into the game. He skated down the left wing before cutting across the low slot and putting a backhander over a sprawling Daccord. Seattle tied the score at 10:13 as Catton lifted a sharp-angled shot from low on the right wing just over Wallstedt's shoulder and inside the near post. The goal came one second after a power play expired. The Wild pulled away with three unanswered goals in the second period. Coleman scored on a breakaway at 2:11 just after he exited the penalty box, beating Daccord with a snap shot low to the glove side. Maatta made it 3-1 at 11:33 with a wrist shot from the left point that found the far upper corner of the net past a screened Daccord. Eriksson Ek added another at 13:00, after Daccord made a save on Matt Boldy's shot from the top of the left faceoff circle. The goalie couldn't quite corral the rebound and Eriksson Ek chipped the puck over Daccord's right shoulder. Kraken forward Jared McCann, the franchise's career scoring leader, didn't play as team officials said he's still being evaluated for a lower-body injury sustained in a 5-3 victory Thursday against Utah. --Field Level Media

item.title: Eleven shot near Florida A&M university in Tallahassee
item.description: A shooting near a Florida university campus in Tallahassee on Saturday night left 11 people with gunshot wounds and another injured, authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A shooting near a Florida university campus in Tallahassee on Saturday night left 11 people with gunshot wounds and another injured, authorities said. The shooting took place near Florida Agricultural & Mechanical University's campus on Perry Street, the university said, while police counted six adults and six juveniles among the injured. "At least three of the shooting victims have sustained serious injuries, while nine others are reported to be in stable condition," the Tallahassee police said in a statement. Initial findings showed a "physical altercation" preceded the shooting, police said, without elaborating. "It is especially heartbreaking to know that children are among those injured," said police chief Lawrence Revell. The youngest of those shot was 11, the NY Post newspaper said, but police did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. An altercation at a homecoming party escalated into gunfire and a fight between two or three individuals led to shots being fired just before 8 p.m., the paper added. Police said their violent crimes unit was investigating the circumstances. "The safety and security of our students, faculty, and staff remain our highest priority," Florida A&M said on X.

item.title: Dmitri Simashev’s first 2 career goals help Mammoth beat Lightning in OT
item.description: Dmitri Simashev scored his first NHL goal and also netted the game-winning tally in overtime, lifting the Utah Mammoth to a 5-4 comeback win over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Saturday night in Salt Lake City.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Dmitri Simashev scored his first NHL goal and also netted the game-winning tally in overtime, lifting the Utah Mammoth to a 5-4 comeback win over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Saturday night in Salt Lake City. After Tampa Bay defenseman J.J. Moser and Utah blue-liner Nate Schmidt were stopped on breakaways in the opening 68 seconds of extra time, Simashev -- also on the rear guard -- slipped in a pass from Barrett Hayton at 1:44 for his first career game-winner. Utah also received goals from Kailer Yamamoto, Dylan Guenther and Anders Lee. Vincent Trocheck had two assists. Mammoth goaltender Karel Vejmelka made 29 saves and earned the secondary assist on Simashev's winner. Jake Guentzel, Pontus Holmberg, Brayden Point and Conor Geekie hit the net for Tampa Bay. In the second half of a back-to-back, goalie Dennis Hildeby made 23 saves for the Lightning, who played without captain Victor Hedman. Nikita Kucherov collected an assist for his 1,138th career point, passing Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead. In the opening period, Guentzel was credited with his seventh goal on a shot into traffic at 5:10 that Utah defenseman Mikhail Sergachev inadvertently put in past Vejmelka. Yamamoto knotted it less than two minutes later when he streaked out and sent a puck in on an odd-man rush. The shot clicked off Hildeby's stick for Yamamoto's third tally. However, Holmberg answered with his third marker a little over three minutes later. In a milestone moment, Kucherov dished out the primary assist to Point on the Lightning's second power play for a 3-1 lead. The historic point prompted the entire visiting bench of players to empty onto the ice and surround the Hart Trophy winner in celebration. The Mammoth also scored on their second power play, as Guenther ripped in his fifth marker to leave the first period trailing 3-2. Vejmelka stopped Point on a breakaway at 1:54 of the second period, but Geekie netted at 5:32 for a 4-2 lead that appeared to put the visitors in full control. However, the Central Division-leading Mammoth rallied behind Lee's third tally and the first NHL goal for Simashev less than three minutes apart for a 4-all tie through 40 minutes ahead of a scoreless third period. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nuggets rally from 23 down to force overtime, beat Pelicans
item.description: Jamal Murray had 42 points, Nikola Jokic finished with 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the host Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to beat the New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jamal Murray had 42 points, Nikola Jokic finished with 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the host Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to beat the New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night. Jokic has 199 career regular-season triple-doubles, second to just-retired Russell Westbrook's 209. Trevon Brazile scored seven of his 17 points in overtime and hit a corner 3-pointer late in the extra period, Christian Braun had 15 points in the game and DeMar DeRozan added 12 points for Denver. Trey Murphy III led the Pelicans with 26 points, Dejounte Murray had 22, Zion Williamson and Derik Queen contributed 17 each, Saddiq Bey scored 14 and Jeremiah Fears added 10. New Orleans led 124-116 with 1:37 left in the fourth quarter before Jokic and Murray hit 3-pointers and Aaron Gordon's dunk made it a two-point game. Murray tied the game at 126 when he was fouled on a 3-point attempt and made 2 of 3 free throws with 16.8 seconds left, sending the game to overtime. Jokic's two free throws in the first minute of overtime gave the Nuggets their first lead since the first quarter. His turnaround jumper in the lane made it 130-128. After Bey split a pair of free throws, Brazile drained a 3-pointer for a 133-129 advantage, and Denver closed it out. The Pelicans raced to a 53-30 lead midway through the second quarter, but the Nuggets rallied in the final six minutes to get within 71-57 before Williamson's dunk in the final second made it a 16-point game at half. New Orleans' lead was 19 heading into the fourth, but the Nuggets rallied. With Murray and Jokic on the bench, Denver cut the deficit to 112-101 on Brazile's 3-pointer with 9:04 left, prompting a New Orleans timeout. The Pelicans extended the lead to 16 points at 118-102, but a 9-0 Nuggets run capped by Brazile's putback dunk made it 118-111. The Nuggets played without Julian Strawther (knee sprain), Spencer Jones (hamstring), Cameron Johnson (sprained ankle) and rookie Alpha Diallo (sprained wrist). New Orleans was without center Yves Missi after he suffered a knee bruise in a loss at Utah on Friday night. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brewers erase 4-run deficit, take 2-0 World Series lead vs. Rays
item.description: MILWAUKEE - Rookie Cooper Pratt made the most of his second opportunity.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE - Rookie Cooper Pratt made the most of his second opportunity. Pratt singled in the go-ahead run to atone for a costly error and the Milwaukee Brewers overcame a four-run deficit behind six scoreless innings from their lockdown bullpen for a 5-4 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Saturday night and a 2-0 lead in the World Series. The Brewers, who trailed 4-0 in the first inning, took their first lead of Game 2 in the seventh when Brice Turang doubled to open off Tyler Wells (0-2) and advanced on a flyout. Pratt greeted Kevin Kelly with an RBI single to right to put Milwaukee up 5-4. "I need to be better defensively, but it's always awesome when you have an opportunity to kind of redeem yourself and make up for it," said the 22-year-old Pratt, inserted into the starting lineup after being called up from Triple-A Nashville in mid-June. "Probably wasn't the best swing, but it did the job and gave us the opportunity to score a run. I'm not going to complain." The Rays stranded the tying run at third in the ninth for the second consecutive game. Jonny DeLuca doubled to open the ninth off Aaron Ashby, who got the final two outs in the eighth. Victor Mesa Jr. struck out and DeLuca advanced to third on a groundout, but Yandy Diaz struck out swinging on a 3-2 count. "It's tough for teams to come in here and play. Our fans are so incredible. It's a tough environment to play in," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. "Tampa Bay had us on the ropes every day. They had runners in scoring position when the game ended both days." Game 3 of the best-of-seven series is Monday in St. Petersburg, Fla. Only 10 teams have overcome a 2-0 deficit to win the World Series, the last being the New York Yankees in 1996. "These Milwaukee fans have been really loud. I know our fans are going to be really loud and excited to see us come back and kind of reset ourselves a little bit," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "We've got a really good pitcher going, as do they. A lot of confidence in this club to respond. They've done it all season long, and they'll continue to do it." Brewers starter Logan Henderson allowed four runs (three earned) on three hits in three innings, but the bullpen picked up its eighth win in nine postseason victories. The eight wins match the 2015 Kansas City Royals for most wins by relievers in a single postseason. JoJo Romero, Dustin May and DL Hall each followed Henderson with a scoreless inning. Abner Uribe (1-0) got four outs and Ashby finished for his third save. Ashby has not allowed a run in 15 2/3 innings over eight postseason appearances. "Our bullpen doesn't get enough credit," Murphy said. "I guess it does get a lot of credit, but you can't say enough great things about them. Six innings of shutout (work) again." Sal Frelick tied it at 4-all with a leadoff homer in the sixth off Ian Seymour. Frelick, who had four homers in 339 at-bats during the regular season, lined a 3-2 fastball 408 feet to center for his second career postseason homer. Milwaukee cut its 4-0 deficit in half with two runs in the bottom of the first, then capitalized on an error to pull within 4-3 in the fourth. Milwaukee threatened in the eighth, but Jackson Chourio was retired home trying to score from third on an infield bouncer on a close play that was upheld upon review. The Brewers, whose only other World Series appearance was as the American League representative in a seven-game loss to St. Louis in 1982, also overcame a 4-0 deficit in the NLCS, rallying for a 6-4 victory over the Dodgers in Game 4 to complete the sweep. Pratt's game-opening error contributed to the Rays' four-run first. Diaz continued to second on Pratt's errant throw from short, then scored on Chandler Simpson's one-out single. Simpson stole second and scored on Junior Caminero's RBI single. Liam Hicks followed with his first postseason homer to put the Rays up 4-0. The Brewers bunched four singles for two runs in the bottom half, including RBI singles by William Contreras and Garrett Mitchell. Milwaukee pulled within 4-3 in the fourth. Pratt battled back from an 0-2 count to draw a one-out walk, advanced to third on Frelick's single and scored on first baseman Jonathan Aranda's fielding error. Chourio prevented a run when his perfect throw home from left field nailed Hicks trying to score from second to end the sixth. That play was also upheld after a review. Rays starter Drew Rasmussen, who was 2-0 with a 1.29 ERA in three previous starts this postseason, allowed three runs on six hits in 3 2/3 innings. --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Kevin Durant leads balanced attack as Rockets take down Hawks
item.description: Kevin Durant led seven double-figure scorers with 22 points as the visiting Houston Rockets beat the Atlanta Hawks 121-114 on Saturday to improve to 3-0.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kevin Durant led seven double-figure scorers with 22 points as the visiting Houston Rockets beat the Atlanta Hawks 121-114 on Saturday to improve to 3-0. The last time Houston opened a season with three straight wins was in 2017-18, when the Rockets went on to post a franchise-record 65 victories and reach the Western Conference finals. Houston extended its winning streak against Atlanta to five games. The teams will meet again Monday in Houston. The Rockets held the high-scoring Hawks, who averaged 130 points while winning their first two games, to a season-low point total. Houston also got 19 points apiece from Tari Eason and Reed Sheppard, who started in place of Fred VanVleet (right knee load management). Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each scored 17 points, with Sengun grabbing 10 rebounds and Thompson collecting 11. Atlanta was led by Jalen Johnson, who fell just shy of a triple-double with 26 points, 16 assists and nine rebounds. Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Dyson Daniels scored 18 points apiece, and CJ McCollum added 17. The Rockets capitalized on Atlanta's struggles from beyond the arc. The Hawks made just 5 of 22 3-point attempts in the first half, including 1 of 10 in the second quarter, and finished 13 of 49 (26.5%) from deep. Houston shot 40% (14 of 35) from 3-point range. The Rockets led by as many as 20 points at 108-88 in the fourth quarter, but Atlanta mounted a late rally with a 9-0 run and cut the deficit to five with 37 seconds remaining. Durant sealed the win with two free throws with 19 seconds left. Atlanta scored the game's first seven points, but Houston responded with a 10-1 run to take a 10-8 lead. The Rockets led 30-26 after the first quarter, fueled by 10 points from Atlanta-area native Jabari Smith Jr. Houston continued to build its advantage, leading by as many as 11 points before taking a 59-48 lead into halftime. The game's start time was pushed back 30 minutes to accommodate the Atlanta Dream's WNBA Finals game Saturday afternoon. The later tipoff did not appear to affect Houston, which did not arrive in Atlanta until after 5 a.m. local time. --Field Level Media

item.title: Portuguese police clear Lisbon housing protest camp, arresting 25
item.description: Portuguese police cleared a camp in central Lisbon held to protest against the country's deepening housing crisis, baton-charging demonstrators in the early hours of Sunday and making 25 arrests.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
item.content:encoded: Portuguese police cleared a camp in central Lisbon held to protest against the country's deepening housing crisis, baton-charging demonstrators in the early hours of Sunday and making 25 arrests. Portugal is grappling with one of Europe's most acute home affordability crises, as prices have more than doubled since 2017 while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, with young people among the hardest hit. The Portuguese protests echo recent demonstrations in [USN:L1N45U0F8 TEXT:"Spain"] over home shortages and surging rents. There have also been protests in cities including [USN:L2N46A01A TEXT:"Paris"], where small student demonstrations over school conditions broadened into wider protests against the government's economic policies. In Portugal, dozens of officers, some with police dogs, moved in on the camp in Rossio Square shortly after 2 a.m. (0200 GMT), having warned protesters their tents would be dismantled if they weren't removed and threatening disobedience charges for those who resisted. POLICE SAY OPERATIONS 'PROPORTIONATE' Protesters had pitched more than 100 tents after Saturday's protest march by thousands along one of Lisbon's main avenues. "We have an obligation to fight for what we believe in," said one marcher, Vitor Gomes, 21, a multimedia communications student, adding that housing speculation, wealth concentration and rising inequality made him pessimistic about the future. Police said the operation was "proportionate" and that 25 people arrested for disobedience were later released and are due in court on Monday. POLICE SAY OFFICERS AND PROTESTERS INJURED A smaller camp of about 50 tents was also dismantled in Porto's Praca D. Joao I, where police made six arrests. While police reported seven minor injuries among officers and protesters in the two operations, activist group Casa para Viver (Homes to Live) said 60 people were hurt and called for a fresh protest outside parliament on Tuesday. "Choosing the early hours of the morning to unleash dogs and baton-charge peaceful protesters is a political decision. It shows this government would rather repress those denouncing the housing crisis than address it," the group said. Protesters say soaring rents and higher living costs are squeezing households and turning housing into a growing source of discontent, with young people among those hardest hit. The Bank of Portugal estimates a shortfall of 300,000 homes nationwide, equivalent to Lisbon's entire housing stock. The protesters are demanding that the government scrap a [USN:L6N45M1AX TEXT:"bill"] to make evictions easier and end rent caps on new leases, which passed a first parliamentary reading, although the far-right Chega party abstained.

item.title: UK's Burnham says he is open to discussing EU free movement
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he wants a discussion about returning to the European Union's freedom of movement rules for workers, a key issue in the 2016 Brexit referendum which led to Britain leaving the bloc.
item.dc:creator: William Schomberg
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he wants a discussion about returning to the European Union's freedom of movement rules for workers, a key issue in the 2016 Brexit referendum which led to Britain leaving the bloc. Building on previous comments about the need to rethink ties with Brussels, Burnham told the Sunday Times that the influx of EU workers into Britain before Brexit had posed very significant challenges. "But, at the same time, it was a type of immigration that perhaps wasn't as difficult (as now)," he said. "Revolving door migration where people would come and then go back is different. The balance of migration has changed, hasn't it, since then? I think we’ve just got to have an honest discussion about those things." Official data has shown [USN:L8N41Y0KA TEXT:"long-term net migration"] in 2025 fell to close to its level before a new post-Brexit immigration system was introduced at the start of 2021. In September, two months after replacing Keir Starmer as Labour Party leader and prime minister, [USN:L1N45M0A5 TEXT:"Burnham said"] Britain should consider options for its relationship with the EU, including possibly rejoining the bloc one day. He had previously backed the pledges of Starmer's government which included no return to freedom of movement which Brussels sets as a condition for being part of the bloc's single market. In his interview with the Sunday Times, conducted on October 19, Burnham said the issue of freedom of movement could be considered as part of a broader reset of Britain's relationship with the EU, including on data sharing and migration. "You've got to see it in the round, rather than just looking at freedom of movement on its own," he said. Burnham - who is trying to find ways to speed up Britain's economy - is due to meet top EU officials for a [USN:S8N44906N TEXT:"summit on November 20"]. He said he could not imagine recommending that Britain adopt the euro currency or the EU's border-free travel arrangements. A new referendum would be needed to rejoin the EU but not necessarily to join the bloc's single market or a customs union, the Sunday Times quoted Burnham as saying. Former Conservative finance minister Jeremy Hunt, who campaigned to stay in the EU in 2016, said it would be a mistake to reopen one of the fundamental debates of the referendum and he said relaxing immigration rules would hurt people in Britain. "I think it will be a hammer blow to getting people off welfare and into work," Hunt told Sky News.

item.title: Cavaliers hold off Nets for first win of season
item.description: Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points and Jarrett Allen had 21 points and eight rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers built a 22-point lead before holding on for a 125-121 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points and Jarrett Allen had 21 points and eight rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers built a 22-point lead before holding on for a 125-121 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Saturday night. Evan Mobley added 20 points and 10 rebounds, and Jaylon Tyson scored 15 points off the bench in Cleveland's home opener. James Harden collected 12 points, eight rebounds and seven assists as the Cavaliers picked up their first win. Brooklyn, which trailed 104-82 with 9:29 remaining, pulled within 123-121 on Michael Porter Jr.'s 3-pointer with 8.1 seconds left. Porter fouled out on the subsequent possession and Sam Merrill made two free throws for the Cavaliers to put them up four points with 5.2 seconds remaining. Porter finished with 28 points and nine rebounds, Julius Randle had 23 points and Egor Demin scored 15 of his 22 points in the fourth quarter for winless Brooklyn. Demin made four 3-pointers in the fourth and had six assists in the game. Peyton Watson had 11 points in his home debut for the Cavaliers, who squandered a 29-point lead Thursday and lost 114-106 to LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers. Chaney Johnson chipped in 10 points for the Nets. Day'Ron Sharpe posted seven points, eight rebounds and six personal fouls before being ejected after two flagrant fouls -- both on Harden 3-point tries -- to earn an automatic ejection. Demin and Watson also fouled out. The Cavaliers took the largest lead of the first half at 68-54 on a Watson layup heading into the break. Mobley, Allen and Porter each scored 13 points in the first half, and Harden had seven points, six rebounds and five assists. Mario Hezonja buried a 3-pointer as time expired in the first quarter, pushing Cleveland's advantage to 35-30. Mobley and Allen had eight points apiece, while Porter paced the Nets with seven points and four rebounds. Mitchell was struck on the head by Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. in the first quarter, briefly delaying the game while he lay under the basket. Brown, who is on a minutes restriction indefinitely because of a left ankle injury, will not play Sunday at home against the Indiana Pacers. The sixth overall pick "is on a long-term plan to build him up properly (physically)," according to coach Jordi Fernandez. Brooklyn was coming off a 110-103 home loss to the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday. Randle and Porter combined for 59 points and were the only Nets in double figures in that game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Obama unloads on Trump while stumping for Democrats ahead of midterms
item.description: Barack Obama framed the Nov. 3 midterm elections vote as a "circuit breaker" to "at least rein in some of the foolishness" of Trump's presidency.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump has been telling voters to view the midterm elections as if he were on the ballot, and on Saturday one of his Democratic predecessors did just that. Ten days out from the elections that will determine control of the closely divided Congress, Barack Obama took to the campaign trail to accuse the Republican president of corruption, deride his strategy for Iran and skewer the gilded aesthetic he has applied to White House renovations. Obama stumped for Democratic candidates at rallies in Cleveland and Detroit, lampooning the Trump administration. Campaigning in Michigan for US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Obama framed the November 3 vote as a "circuit breaker" to "at least rein in some of the foolishness" of Trump's presidency. "We got to flip that circuit breaker, bring some accountability to this government," Obama said. Obama, president from 2009 until Trump began his first term in 2017, remains one of the most popular figures among Democrats. They hope that bringing him into the race can fire up their supporters for a tight US Senate race in which El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers, a former US representative. The former president obliged the Michigan crowd by playing to Democrats' frequently repeated criticisms of Trump and of Republicans' willingness to go along with him. "We have never seen a president excel in straight-up grifting, on your dime, like this," Obama said. "Never seen a president so intent on selling favors like this ... Now the party seems to stand for corrupt government, or inept government, or no government." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. But in a Truth Social post on early Sunday morning, Trump called Obama a "grossly incompetent President" and labeled El-Sayed a "Muslim Brotherhood Jihadist, who hates Jews and Blacks and AMERICANS and TRUMP". A Reuters/Ipsos poll in August found that 63% of Americans think the president and his family have [USN:L6N44F13X TEXT:"inappropriately profited"] from cryptocurrency since he returned to the White House last year and that 69% believe his policy decisions are influenced by his private business dealings. Obama also ridiculed the administration's claims of victory against Iran. He argued that the war has given Iran more economic leverage because its threats to attack shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have unsettled oil exporters. "Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz, where oil goes through to get to the world," Obama said. In his social media post, Trump derided the Obama administration's approach to the Iranians, saying that he "paid off Iran with $Billions, and gave them a road to a Nuclear Weapon" with his 2015 [USN:L6N42K0ZD TEXT:"Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action"] accord with Iran. The United States withdrew from the 2015 agreement during Trump's first term. The former president also accused the Trump administration of emphasizing unimportant matters, sarcastically calling Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth someone "laser-focused on important matters like the jawline and testosterone levels of our troops" and ridiculing White House renovations as tacky. "He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory," Obama said.

item.title: Joel Embiid posts triple-double, 76ers handle Bucks
item.description: Joel Embiid recorded his 10th career triple-double and Jaylen Brown scored 27 points on his 30th birthday to lead the Philadelphia 76ers to a 127-116 home win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joel Embiid recorded his 10th career triple-double and Jaylen Brown scored 27 points on his 30th birthday to lead the Philadelphia 76ers to a 127-116 home win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday. Embiid finished with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for Philadelphia, which rested LeBron James (back/sciatica). James is expected to play Sunday against the Detroit Pistons, while Embiid will rest in the second half of a back-to-back. Tyrese Maxey pitched in with 26 points for the Sixers, while VJ Edgecombe made five 3-pointers as part of a 17-point, 13-rebound performance. While the Sixers are 3-0 on the young season, the Bucks fell to 0-3 despite eight players scoring in double figures. Jaime Jaquez Jr. led Milwaukee with 21 points, while Kel'el Ware had 19 points and 13 rebounds off the bench for the visitors. The teams were tied at 82-82 with four minutes left in the third quarter before the Sixers ended the period on a 15-5 push. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Maxey each made a 3-pointer during that surge, which Maxey capped with a tough fadeaway with the quarter winding down. Philadelphia started to pull away early in the fourth. Embiid's jumper gave the hosts a 113-98 lead with six minutes left. The Sixers still held a comfortable advantage at 117-108 with 3:18 to go before the Bucks rattled off six in a row in just over a minute to make it a three-point game. However, Edgecombe came up with a big offensive rebound on the other end, leading to a 3-pointer by Brown. Then on the next Philadelphia possession, Brown found Caldwell-Pope for a 3-pointer that essentially sealed the outcome. Philadelphia knocked down five 3-pointers in the first quarter -- three by Edgecombe -- en route to a 34-25 lead after 12 minutes. The Sixers struggled to find a rhythm in the second quarter, as they shot just 33.3% from the field (9 of 27). Brown led all scorers with 16 points in the first half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ville Koivunen scores OT winner as Penguins rally past Predators
item.description: Ville Koivunen scored with 1:16 left in overtime for the ailing Pittsburgh Penguins, who rallied to take down the visiting Nashville Predators 3-2 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ville Koivunen scored with 1:16 left in overtime for the ailing Pittsburgh Penguins, who rallied to take down the visiting Nashville Predators 3-2 on Saturday night. Connor Dewar and Rickard Rakell also scored for the Penguins, who won their second straight game. Arturs Silovs finished with 24 saves for Pittsburgh, marking the first time the team has won consecutive games since starting the season 2-0. Steven Stamkos scored his fifth of the season and Jayden Struble notched his first for the Predators, who are 0-4 in overtime and shootout games. Juuse Saros made a season-high 34 saves, but Rakell spoiled his bid for a victory by tying the game with 1:06 remaining in regulation. Pittsburgh played without Evgeni Malkin, who missed the game due to an illness. Malkin's longtime teammates, though, made sure the Penguins earned at least a point. With Silovs on the bench for an extra attacker, Sidney Crosby controlled the puck in the left faceoff circle. Instead of shooting, he fed Rakell at the other circle and Rakell buried it before Saros could glide across the crease. Saros had stopped Rakell twice on breakaways earlier in the game, including a short-handed chance with less than eight minutes left. Nashville coach Andrew Brunette moved Matthew Wood onto the top line alongside Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly following Thursday's 6-0 loss at Boston. The trio produced the game's opening goal at 9:24 of the first period when Wood's shot deflected off Stamkos' skate. Pittsburgh capitalized on a Predators turnover to draw even early in the second period. Adam Wilsby's failed clearance behind the net allowed Dewar to tie the game just 18 seconds into the period. It was one of 24 giveaways for Nashville. Struble, acquired from Montreal on Oct. 9 for a second-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft, restored Nashville's lead at 6:40 of the second period. Besides Malkin missing the game, Pittsburgh has six skaters on injured reserve. Egor Chinakhov also missed his second straight game due to a lower-body injury. --Field Level Media

item.title: Drake Batherson (hat trick), Senators too strong for Rangers
item.description: Drake Batherson scored a hat trick and added an assist as the Ottawa Senators topped the visiting New York Rangers 7-4 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Drake Batherson scored a hat trick and added an assist as the Ottawa Senators topped the visiting New York Rangers 7-4 on Saturday night. Jake Sanderson tallied one goal and added two assists, while Dylan Cozens and Michael Amadio each scored and chipped in a helper for Ottawa. Tim Stutzle also found the back of the net as the Senators improved to 5-2-0 on home ice. Jonas Johansson, making his Senators and season debut, made 24 saves. J.T. Miller and Will Cuylle each scored and added an assist, and Alexis Lafreniere and Pavel Dorofeyev also scored for the Rangers, who are 1-3-1 in their last five. Adam Fox and Noah Laba each added a pair of helpers, and Dylan Garand stopped 17 shots for New York. Trailing 5-3, Dorofeyev got the Rangers to within one, one-timing a Cuylle feed past Johansson for his third goal this season at 15:32 of the third. Amadio scored into an empty net with 1:14 remaining for his third of the season. Batherson completed the hat trick with an empty-netter at 19:48 of the third. Sanderson gave the Senators a 5-3 lead at 13:38 of the third, backhanding the rebound off Ridly Greig's shot for his first of the season. Lafreniere pulled the Rangers to 4-3 with 26 seconds remaining in the second period, snapping home a 2-on-1 feed from Miller for his ninth of the season. Trailing 4-1, New York cut the lead in half as Miller batted home a bouncing puck for his third of the season at 12:54 of the second period. The Senators took a 4-1 lead at 11:21 as Batherson's centering pass directed off Cozens' skate and past Garand. Cuylle got the Rangers on the board, short-handed, at the midway mark of the second, snapping a Laba feed past Johansson. Batherson added his second of the night to give the Sens a 3-0 lead at 1:47 of the middle frame, putting home the rebound off Cozens' shot. The Senators jumped out to an early 2-0 lead, scoring twice in a 1:06 span of the first period. Ottawa opened the scoring at 5:33 of the first as Batherson snapped a Sanderson feed short-side past Garand. Stutzle doubled the Senators' lead at 6:39, tapping in a cross-ice feed from Fabian Zetterlund. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bruins tally 4 in the 3rd to edge Sharks, extend unbeaten streak to 8
item.description: The Boston Bruins scored four third-period goals, including three in a row to erase a 3-2 deficit, to edge the visiting San Jose Sharks 6-4 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Boston Bruins scored four third-period goals, including three in a row to erase a 3-2 deficit, to edge the visiting San Jose Sharks 6-4 on Saturday night. David Pastrnak tied former teammate Patrice Bergeron for third on Boston's all-time goals list (427) to kick off the late-game surge. Fraser Minten (game-winner), James Hagens and Casey Mittelstadt all had a goal and an assist, while Marat Khusnutdinov and Will Borgen also lit the lamp for the Bruins, who are 7-0-1 in their last eight games. Boston's Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka each dished out two assists, and Jeremy Swayman made 23 saves. Michael Misa, Kiefer Sherwood, Dmitry Orlov and Will Smith each scored a goal, Jacob Trouba had two assists, and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 29 shots for San Jose, which was on a two-game win streak. Orlov's one-time blast from the center point off an Ivar Stenberg pass gave San Jose its first lead of the night at 3-2 4:03 into the third, but two goals in 40 seconds put the Bruins back in front. Pastrnak jumped right out of the box from a tripping penalty and tied the game at 8:27, taking Peterka's feed into the top of the right circle and firing off a wrister past Nedeljkovic's blocker. Hagens gave Boston a 4-3 lead when he followed up Lindholm's chance in front at 9:07. With the Bruins on a four-minute power play, Minten added an insurance marker at 12:00, burying a rebound after Nedeljkovic robbed Peterka. San Jose would not go quietly. Smith made it a one-goal game again with a 4-on-4 goal with 7:33 left in regulation, slotting home Trouba's feed to the right circle after Macklin Celebrini circled the zone with the puck. With 30 seconds to go, Borgen finished into an empty net. Mittelstadt opened the scoring with his 100th career goal only 3:08 into the opening period, finishing off a relentless shift with Lindholm and Hagens by netting a loose puck from outside the right crease. San Jose's power play evened the score at 5:54. Tyler Toffoli's shot from above the right circle was deflected and found the stick of Misa, who slotted it into a virtually open net from the left side. Strong net-front play allowed the Bruins to jump back in front at 8:20 of the second. After Minten found Morgan Geekie between the circles, Khusnutdinov slipped in from the left side and buried a backhand high to Nedeljkovic's glove side. Swayman denied Sherwood's partial short-handed breakaway off a turnover earlier in the period, but could not stop a second as the Sharks made it 2-2 at 13:34. Sherwood broke up Lindholm's pass in the neutral zone and broke in ahead, putting home a top-shelf shot. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alpine F1 team defends Colapinto after Clarkson comments
item.description: The Alpine Formula One team issued a statement in support of their driver after Jeremy Clarkson joked that he would give him a grid penalty just for being Argentine.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: The Alpine Formula One team issued a statement in support of driver Franco Colapinto on Saturday after TV celebrity Jeremy Clarkson joked that he would give him a grid penalty just for being Argentine. Clarkson, famed for presenting British motoring programmes "Top Gear" and Amazon's "The Grand Tour" as well as the farming hit "Clarkson's Farm," made his comments in an interview with Sky Sports television ahead of the US Grand Prix. Colapinto has a 10-place grid penalty for Sunday's race at the Circuit of the Americas as a result of power unit component changes. "Franco's got a grid penalty for being Argentinian," said Clarkson, a guest of Alpine in Austin. "Probably. Well, I'd give him one for that. "That's just because of what happened when we went there," he added. Clarkson went to Argentina's Patagonia with Top Gear in 2014 in a controversial episode that triggered protests after he drove a car with a registration number that some saw as a reference to the 1982 war over the Falkland Islands that Argentina claims sovereignty over and knows as Las Malvinas. "We're aware of the comments made in a recent TV interview from a guest of the team in Austin," Renault-owned Alpine said, without mentioning Clarkson. "We would like to reiterate that these are personal views and do not align with the team's values of promoting kindness and respect. Franco is our driver and has our full support." Colapinto has a legion of Argentine fans and has had to repeatedly issue statements calling for restraint after rivals and even his own teammates received online abuse. The Argentine said in Austin earlier in the week that the bad comments had "crossed a few lines lately" and said his mechanics and engineers had been targeted by some supporters seeking blame for race incidents. "My mechanics got a lot of hate, my engineer, people from my team that want me to do well and help me perform," he said. "And I'm working with daily getting these kind of messages." Colapinto's manager Jamie Campbell-Walter posted on X that "Jeremy Clarkson’s comments about Franco’s nationality were completely unacceptable. There is no place for remarks like this in Formula One, regardless of who makes them or whether they are intended as a joke. "We have worked hard to promote respect and put an end to hostility and abuse. That respect must go both ways. We cannot ask anyone to behave responsibly while accepting comments like these from prominent figures visiting our sport."

item.title: Serbia votes in historic election as students seek to end Vucic's long grip on power
item.description: Serbian voters turned out in force on Sunday as a mass student protest movement sought to unseat longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in the biggest challenge to his rule for more than a decade.
item.dc:creator: Ivana Sekularac, Edward Mcallister, Aleksandar Vasovic
item.content:encoded: Serbian voters turned out in force on Sunday as a mass student protest movement sought to unseat longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in the biggest challenge to his rule for more than a decade. The [USN:L8N46618N TEXT:"snap parliamentary elections"], called by Vucic in September, come after almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and creeping authoritarianism triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024. The students have since [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"gained widespread support"]. Unusually long lines snaked from polling stations in cities and towns across the country. Pollsters and monitors CeSID and Ipsos put turnout at 27.3% by 11 a.m. (1000 GMT), nearly double the 15.1% at the same time in the previous election in 2023. Even Vucic waited in line for nearly two hours to vote. First indications of results are expected around two hours after polls close at 8 p.m. (1900 GMT). A student victory would be a profound political shift in the Balkan country of some 6 million people, reminiscent of the [USN:L1N40V01B TEXT:"defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban"] in April. It could also offer a blueprint for other student movements across Europe, which have [USN:L6N464038 TEXT:"taken to the streets"] in recent weeks to protest, [USN:L2N46A01A TEXT:"in some cases violently"], against poor education standards and a lack of prospects. "It is very important for all people to come and vote if they want to change something and I think it is a time for change," said lawyer Marija Cvjeticanin at a Belgrade polling station. Vucic, who resigned from his second term as president to run again for prime minister, is a strong incumbent. Many voters thank him for pulling Serbia from economic obscurity and orchestrating a period of sustained modernisation including new highways, railways, schools and hospitals. OPINION POLLS PREDICT TIGHT RACE Vucic has pledged higher pensions and public sector salaries, and investment in state healthcare. Internationally, he has sought closer ties with China, a major investor, and remained close to Russia, Serbia's traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas. At the same time, he still says he wants to join the European Union, Serbia's largest trading partner, but the bloc has become [USN:L6N3Z90I6 TEXT:"increasingly frustrated"] with a lack of reform. "I voted for our children, our young people...our children deserve peace and work, only Vucic can bring that," said Hatidza, a Roma woman. The students' domestic agenda aims to root out graft and improve schooling, but they have been quieter on their international ambitions. Their list of 250 largely unknown candidates includes university professors, actors and farmers, and is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, although it is not clear who would be prime minister should they win. "I hope that today will pass in a democratic atmosphere, in peace, and that we will legitimately elect a new government in Serbia," Srdanovic said after casting his vote in Novi Sad, adding that the scenes suggested there would be a record voter turnout in the country's recent history. After casting his vote, Vucic said he would respect the result. "If we lose we will acknowledge the will of the electorate, if we win no one will take it (from us)," he said. Opinion polls ahead of the vote predicted a tight race. The head of the Election Commission, Vladimir Dimitrijevic, said voting had so far passed without incident, but monitoring bodies CeSID and CRTA pointed to incidents related to the electoral roll and secrecy of voting. STUDENT PROTESTS INCREASE PRESSURE ON VUCIC The student-led street protests sparked by the station disaster quickly became the biggest in a generation, calling for Vucic to step down. Rights groups and activists say [USN:L8N4612LD TEXT:"repression has worsened"] in the period since. "For decades the people have been waiting for this time, something to bring hope that we can live freely and by the rules of democracy," said actor Jelena Stupljanin, 48, at a Belgrade polling station. Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) have repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents. He says the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students dismiss. "This has been one of the most difficult but the most emotional campaigns," Vucic told his supporters on Thursday. "We stood against those who wanted to destroy Serbia."

item.title: Saudi says Riyadh airport partly reopens despite renewed Houthi threats
item.description: Saudi Arabia said its main airport resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday even as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis vowed to keep striking the facility, saying it remained a "military target".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia said its main airport resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday even as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis vowed to keep striking the facility, saying it remained a "military target". King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had halted operations on October 10 following an attack claimed by the Houthis that killed 13 people, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. Saudi Arabia intercepted another wave of missiles and drones on Sunday as fighting with the militant group continued unabated. The conflict has become an increasingly destabilising element in the US-Israeli offensive against Iran , turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war. FLIGHT TRACKING DATA SHOWS LITTLE TRAFFIC After Saudi authorities announced the partial resumption of operations at the airport, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree vowed the facility would "never be safe" and urged airlines, airport staff and travellers not to use it. Late on Saturday, the airport said Terminal 1 would be designated for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international flights operated by national carriers starting Sunday. Despite the announcement, flight tracking data from Flightradar24 showed little traffic at the airport on Sunday. The Saudi-led coalition said earlier this month that the Houthis had carried out 20 attacks on the airport between October 1 and 11. MISSILE AND DRONE ATTACKS CONTINUE Saudi civil defense said on Sunday that shrapnel from the interception of two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis over Khamis Mushait and Ahad Rafidah injured two people and damaged residential buildings and vehicles. Civil defense authorities earlier issued emergency alerts for Riyadh and the cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran on Sunday, before saying minutes later that the danger had passed. The coalition said two drones and a ballistic missile were launched towards Riyadh, and a cruise missile towards the southern city of Khamis Mushait. It later said it intercepted 10 ballistic missiles fired towards southern Saudi Arabia. The Houthis said they attacked the airport and Saudi oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi authorities did not comment directly on the Houthi statements. Saudi Arabia has stepped up its strikes against the Houthis after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month, closing in on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait – a global maritime chokepoint and shipping route for Gulf oil producers on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula to the Strait of Hormuz. The renewed fighting in Yemen has shattered a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022. Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of a coalition supporting the internationally recognised government, after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa a year earlier.

item.title: North Korea's Kim Jong Un returns from China after war memorial visit, state media says
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un returned from a surprise one-day trip to the Chinese border city of Dandong, where he visited a historic Korean War memorial, North Korean state media said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Cynthia Kim, Joyce Lee
item.content:encoded: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un returned from a [USN:L1N46A01U TEXT:"surprise one-day trip"] to the Chinese border city of Dandong, where he visited a historic Korean War memorial, North Korean state media said on Sunday. Kim visited the city on Saturday and returned by road, crossing a newly opened bridge that connects North Korea to its biggest international backer and trading partner. The quick trip symbolised a push by Beijing and Pyongyang to expand trade ties. North Korean state media emphasised the historical weight of the visit, which came a day before the anniversary of China joining the Korean War on Pyongyang's side. The bilateral relationship is an "unbreakable" bond forged during the 1950-1953 conflict between North Korea and the US-backed South, state media said. The two Koreas are technically still at war after the conflict ended in an armistice, rather than a peace treaty. Kim said during his tour that the North Korean people would "forever remember the glorious years of fighting alongside the Chinese people" and pass down "generational gratitude to the Chinese people who helped our revolution with blood", state news agency KCNA reported. Beijing and Pyongyang have been seeking to [USN:L1N46A01U TEXT:"bolster their economic relationship"] ahead of a trip to the region by US President Donald Trump next month. It also highlights a delicate diplomatic balancing act by Pyongyang, which has also been deepening [USN:L4N44L021 TEXT:"military ties"] with Russia in the past two years. Guided by Wang Huning, the fourth-highest-ranking official in the Chinese Communist Party, Kim visited Dandong's Memorial Hall of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, accompanied by a high-level North Korean delegation that included his sister, Kim Yo Jong, and Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui. Touring the memorial, Kim viewed an archival photograph of his grandfather, North Korean founder Kim Il Sung, and Mao Zedong, founder of the modern Chinese state, footage from North Korea's state-run television KRT showed. Kim presented a commemorative plaque featuring Kim Il Sung as a gift to the museum before holding a formal meeting with Wang and inspecting a bus factory in Dandong. Kim last visited Beijing in September 2025 for a military parade, and Chinese President Xi Jinping visited North Korea in June. "Enjoying a bird's-eye view at the middle point of the newly inaugurated bridge, Comrade Kim Jong Un expressed expectation that the bridge would undoubtedly and correctly fulfill its historic mission of linking the two countries and firmly joining the minds of the peoples of the two countries," KCNA reported.

item.title: Top 25 roundup: UCF hands No. 2 BYU first loss in double OT
item.description: Keyone Jenkins threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Grayson Brousseau to open the second overtime, then connected with Tyren Hornes for a two-point conversion to give UCF a wild 39-31 win over mistake-prone No. 2 BYU on Saturday afternoon in Orlando, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Keyone Jenkins threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Grayson Brousseau to open the second overtime, then connected with Tyren Hornes for a two-point conversion to give UCF a wild 39-31 win over mistake-prone No. 2 BYU on Saturday afternoon in Orlando, Fla. The Knights' defense stopped BYU on fourth down in the second overtime after the Cougars advanced to the UCF 4-yard line. Earlier, BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier connected with Legend Glasker for a 28-yard touchdown pass to open the first overtime. Jenkins answered with a scrambling 25-yard touchdown pass to Josh Derry on UCF's possession to force a second extra period. Jenkins passed for 293 yards and three touchdowns as the Knights (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) defeated the highest-ranked opponent in program history. Hornes had six catches for 137 yards. Bachmeier threw for 257 yards and a touchdown and also ran for a score. Kyler Kasper caught six passes for 129 yards for BYU (6-1, 3-1). Overtime was necessary after Jenkins was stopped short on a quarterback sneak from the BYU 1-yard line with 1:42 remaining in regulation. UCF got one more possession, but Will Stone's 46-yard field-goal attempt was blocked by Faletau Satuala to end the fourth quarter. No. 1 Miami 52, Pittsburgh 23 Malachi Toney caught a program-record 16 passes for 194 yards and three touchdowns to lead the Hurricanes to a comfortable Atlantic Coast Conference win against the Panthers in Miami Gardens, Fla. Toney finished the first half with 11 catches for 147 yards to secure his sixth career double-digit catch game. The Hurricanes remain unbeaten after their first game as the top-ranked team in the nation since 2002. Miami (7-0, 5-0 ACC) quarterback Darian Mensah was efficient once again, completing 31 of 37 passes for 387 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions. Pitt (5-3, 2-3) dropped its third consecutive game since losing quarterback Mason Heintschel for the season after he tore his ACL. Holden Geriner made his second start in Pitt's past three games. He completed 18 of 32 passes for 268 yards and one touchdown. No. 6 Indiana 13, Michigan 6 (OT) Josh Hoover scored on a 4-yard keeper in overtime to lift the Hoosiers to a Big Ten victory over Michigan in Ann Arbor, Mich. Turbo Richard rushed 19 times for 68 yards and Lee Beebe Jr. added 56 yards on 12 carries for Indiana (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten), which had not won at Michigan since 1967. Hoover completed 8 of 18 passes for 81 yards and his first interception of the year while Nico Radicic booted two field goals. Freshman quarterback Tommy Carr hit 20 of 32 passes for 167 yards in his first start for Michigan (4-3, 1-3). JJ Buchanan caught six passes for 57 yards and Trey Butkowski kicked two field goals, including a 26-yarder on the final play of regulation. No. 19 Texas 34, No. 7 Ole Miss 27 Arch Manning passed for 212 yards and accounted for three touchdowns and Raleek Brown amassed 157 rushing yards as the Longhorns outlasted the Rebels in a crucial Southeastern Conference clash in Austin, Texas. Trailing 24-3 at halftime, the Rebels roared back to score three touchdowns and limit the Longhorns to just 19 yards of offense in the first 16:03 of the second half. Trinidad Chambliss led Ole Miss (5-2, 3-2 SEC) with 250 yards passing. He threw two touchdowns to Horatio Fields but also produced a career-high three interceptions. But Texas (5-2, 2-2) turned to its ground attack late to cement the victory. Brown ripped off a 47-yard run to set the table for Manning's 1-yard TD on a naked bootleg that put the Longhorns on top for good, snapping their two-game losing streak which dropped them from No. 1 in the AP poll. Cincinnati 37, No. 8 Texas Tech 24 Quarterback JC French IV threw for four touchdowns and Cole Tabb ran for a career-high 173 yards and a score as the host Bearcats posted their biggest upset in nearly 20 years with a Big 12 victory over the Red Raiders. After squandering an opportunity last weekend at West Virginia, the Bearcats (5-2, 2-2 Big 12) completed a 180-degree turn by dominating the Red Raiders (6-1, 3-1) to snap a two-game losing streak. It marked the Bearcats' largest win over a ranked foe since they beat No. 7 Rutgers 30-11 on Nov. 18, 2006. It also served as the fourth win over a Top 10 foe in school history. French, who completed 19 of 30 passes for 172 yards, threw for three scores in the final 7:48 of the first half to turn a 6-3 deficit into a 24-6 halftime lead. Peyton Morgan picked off French and returned it 53 yards for a touchdown with 8:49 remaining in the quarter to cut the deficit to 24-15. Cincinnati responded with a nine-play, 80-yard drive that French capped with a 17-yard pass to Larenzo Fenner. No. 9 UCLA 28, Michigan State 10 Ty Dieffenbach threw for 198 yards and a touchdown while the Bruins held the Spartans to 156 yards of offense in Pasadena, Calif. Dieffenbach completed 18 of 31 passes and Anthony Woods added 112 yards on 14 carries, plus a touchdown. Dieffenbach found Brian Rowe Jr. for a catch-and-run 63-yard score two minutes into the third quarter and Anthony Woods (112 rushing yards) capped a 10-play, 70-yard drive on a 4-yard run later in the period. UCLA (7-0, 5-0) recorded four sacks and six tackles for loss. Michigan State used two quarterbacks and neither one was particularly effective. Leo Hannan was 9 of 15 for 67 yards with an interception, while Kayd Coffman completed 4 of 10 passes for 42 yards with a score and a pick. The Spartans (2-6, 0-5 Big Ten) rushed for only 47 yards on 29 carries and converted just 2 of 11 third downs. Kenneth Williams did give Michigan State an early lead with a 14-yard touchdown run. No. 10 Utah 21, No. 14 Houston 13 Quarterback Devon Dampier ran for a season-high 150 yards and two touchdowns on 15 carries to rally the Utes to a victory over the Cougars in Salt Lake City. Dampier also threw for 204 yards and had two interceptions. The Utes (7-0, 4-0 Big 12) are one of three FBS teams that remain undefeated, rallying from a 10-0 hole midway through the third quarter. Conner Weigman threw for 282 yards to lead Houston (6-2, 3-2). Amare Thomas racked up a season-high-tying 133 yards on five catches for the Cougars. South Carolina 27, No. 11 Tennessee 24 Malik Orsan kicked a 48-yard field goal on the game's final play as the Gamecocks rallied to win their second straight conference game by edging the Volunteers in Columbia, S.C. Tomiwa Durojaiye recovered a fumble following a sack in the final minute, setting up Orsan's winning kick as the Gamecocks (4-3, 2-3 SEC) overcame a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit. LaNorris Sellers was 18 of 32 for 210 yards with a touchdown and an interception; he also rushed for 96 yards on 18 attempts with two more scores. Tennessee (6-2, 3-2) had 120 yards on 32 carries and a score from DeSean Bishop, who delivered his fourth straight 100-yard outing. Tight end DaSaahn Brame and wide receiver Mike Matthews rushed for scores. George MacIntyre was 16-of-23 passing for 136 yards. No. 12 Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 17 Kenny Minchey threw for one touchdown and rushed for another as the Wildcats overcame an early 10-point deficit to defeat the Commodores in Lexington, Ky. Willie Rodriguez caught six passes for 67 yards and added a rushing score, while Ty Bryant notched his fourth interception in the last three games for the Wildcats (7-1, 5-1 SEC). Brennen Ward added a rushing score and DJ Miller caught a touchdown pass for Kentucky. Minchey completed 19 of 26 passes for 203 yards as Kentucky won its sixth straight game. The Wildcats have registered five consecutive SEC victories for the first time since 1977. Jared Curtis completed 27 of 36 passes for 247 yards, two touchdowns and one interception for the Commodores (3-5, 0-5), who lost their fifth consecutive game. Jayvontay Conner and Ja'Cory Thomas caught touchdown passes and Junior Sherrill had eight receptions for 78 yards for Vanderbilt, which led 10-0 before Kentucky rattled off three touchdowns in less than 10 minutes of game time spanning the second and third quarters. No. 13 Alabama 31, Texas A&M 20 Keelon Russell threw two of his three touchdown passes in the fourth quarter to help the Crimson Tide pull away late in a win over the Aggies in Tuscaloosa, Ala. Russell, who threw one touchdown pass and two interceptions in his previous two games combined, amassed 311 yards through the air with one interception for the Crimson Tide (6-2, 4-2 SEC). Rico Scott stepped up with six catches for 156 yards for Alabama, which snapped its two-game losing streak. Marcel Reed completed 14 of 21 passes for 163 yards, one TD and two interceptions for Texas A&M (4-4, 1-4), which has already lost as many SEC games this year as it did the last two seasons combined. Minnesota 13, No. 15 Iowa 10 Luke Drzewiecki drilled a 46-yard field goal as time expired to lift the Golden Gophers to a win over the Hawkeyes in Minneapolis. Minnesota (5-2, 3-1 Big Ten) shined on defense with three interceptions and a fumble recovery. Darius Taylor rushed for the Golden Gophers' lone touchdown, and Drake Lindsey completed 14 of 26 passes for 137 yards and an interception. Hank Brown completed 11 of 21 passes for 136 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions for Iowa (5-2, 2-2), which tied the game with 3:46 left on a 37-yard touchdown catch by Reece Vander Zee. Wisconsin 24, No. 16 Southern California 7 Bryan Jackson II scored the go-ahead touchdown against his former team and the Badgers' defense limited the Trojans to 241 total yards during a stifling victory in Madison, Wisc. Colton Joseph added a touchdown pass and tight end Ryan Schwendeman tacked on a game-sealing touchdown run as Wisconsin (5-2, 3-1 Big Ten) physically controlled most of the last three quarters, finishing with a 142 to minus-17 edge in rushing yards. USC QB Jayden Maiava was basically forced to go it alone. He completed 31 of 50 passes for 258 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions but he was sacked five times. Taniela Tupou had a 4-yard touchdown catch which briefly gave the Trojans (6-2, 3-2) a 7-3 lead in the second quarter. No. 18 LSU 38, Auburn 17 Sam Leavitt threw for three touchdowns and ran for a fourth as LSU routed host Auburn for an SEC win. Leavitt completed 32 of 45 passes for a career-high 387 yards as LSU outgained Auburn 552-271. Jackson Harris caught nine passes for 178 yards and two scores for LSU (6-2, 3-2 SEC), which ended an eight-game losing streak in SEC road games dating back to the 2024 season. Byrum Brown passed for 160 yards and rushed for a team-high 21 yards and a touchdown on 19 carries for Auburn (4-3, 2-3), which never led one week after upsetting top-ranked Georgia. No. 21 Boise State 31, Washington State 10 Dylan Riley rushed for a game-high 128 yards, including a pair of fourth-quarter touchdowns, and the Broncos scored 21 unanswered points in the final 13:33 to pull away for a victory over the Cougars in Pullman, Wash. Riley, who carried 13 times, scored on runs of 33 and 72 yards for Boise State (6-1, 3-0 Pac-12), who won their sixth consecutive game. Sire Gaines added 64 yards rushing and a score on 10 attempts. Maddux Madsen completed 14 of 23 passes for 149 yards and a touchdown, with Rasean Jones making five catches for 69 yards. Quarterback Owen Eshelman, making his second start for Washington State (1-7, 0-4), was 21-of-40 passing for 191 yards with one interception. He also rushed for a team-high 33 yards on 23 attempts. No. 23 SMU 59, Cal 20 Kendrick Raphael rushed for 104 yards and two touchdowns against his former team to help the Mustangs pull away from the Golden Bears for an ACC win in Dallas. Raphael, who rushed for 943 yards and 13 touchdowns for Cal last season, also snared a touchdown pass from Kevin Jennings, who completed 16 of 23 attempts for 223 yards and three touchdowns. Christian Rhodes added two short touchdown runs for SMU (6-1, 4-1 ACC), which outscored Cal 42-0 in the second half after trailing by three at halftime. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completed 27 of 37 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown for Cal (3-5, 2-3), which scored first when it moved the ball 65 yards in seven plays on its opening drive. Sagapolutele capped the march with a 10-yard touchdown pass to Chase Hendricks. No. 24 Northwestern 42, Rutgers 14 Aidan Chiles threw three touchdowns and ran for two scores as the Wildcats raced out to a big lead in the first half and rolled to a Big Ten victory in Evanston, Ill. Northwestern (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten) earned its fourth straight win as Chiles completed 19 of 25 passes for 219 yards and added 83 rushing yards. Caleb Komolafe rushed for 150 yards, which included a 33-yard score that put the Wildcats up 28-3 late in the first half. Griffin Wilde added nine catches for 133 yards and a score. Antwan Raymond rushed for a season-high 150 yards and Clay Thevenin added 116 yards for Rutgers (2-5, 1-3), which lost its 46th consecutive game against a ranked opponent. Starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan played just three snaps before getting hurt on a scramble. Backup AJ Surace completed 7 of 18 passes for 64 yards. No. 25 Arizona 39, Iowa State 3 The Wildcats scored on their first four possessions to cruise to a win over the Cyclones in Tucson, Ariz. Arizona QB Noah Fifita threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns on 27-of-34 passing, increasing his career TD passes to 91, first among active FBS players. His younger brother Dash Fifita, a first-year linebacker, had 2.5 tackles for loss and two sacks, while receiver Isaiah Mizell caught eight passes for 134 yards and a score. The Wildcats (6-1, 3-1 Big 12) are bowl eligible in consecutive years for the first time since 2014-15. Iowa State (3-4, 1-3) dropped to 0-4 against ranked teams this season, finishing with 221 yards to Arizona's 477. Cyclones quarterback Jaylen Raynor (8-for-10 passing for 106 yards) was benched at halftime for Connor Moberly (7 of 17, 63 yards). Running back Aidan Flora, who began the day second in the Big 12 in rushing yards per game, finished with only 36 yards on 12 carries. --Field Level Media

item.title: Devils limit Kings to 13 shots, register third consecutive win
item.description: Arseny Gritsyuk scored for the fifth straight game to help the New Jersey Devils seal a 3-1 win against the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday afternoon in Newark, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Arseny Gritsyuk scored for the fifth straight game to help the New Jersey Devils seal a 3-1 win against the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday afternoon in Newark, N.J. Anthony Mantha and Brett Pesce also scored, and Jake Allen made 12 saves for New Jersey, which has won three straight and five of the past six. Scott Laughton scored and Anton Forsberg made 23 saves for the Kings, who had won two in a row following a 0-4-2 start to the season. Pesce gave the Devils a 2-1 lead at 8:08 of the third period. The veteran defenseman had the time and space to hold the puck and wait for Kings forward Andre Lee to slide by before scoring with a wrist shot from above the right hash marks. The Kings briefly thought they tied it with 4:36 left on a deflection by Trevor Moore, but it was quickly ruled on the ice that he had used a high stick and confirmed on review. Gritsyuk scored into an empty net with 1:05 left for a 3-1 lead. Forsberg helped keep the game scoreless by making back-to-back pad saves without his goal stick at 12:03 and 12:12 of the second period. Shortly afterward, the Devils were on a power play when Kings forward Joel Armia stuck out his stick blade and prevented the puck from sliding over the goal line after it got behind Forsberg. Laughton came out of the box on the same penalty and stayed on the ice before receiving an Adrian Kempe pass from below the goal line and scoring via a one-timer for a 1-0 lead at 15:57 of the second. Mantha tied it 1-1 at 18:43 of the second. Jesper Boqvist circled behind the Los Angeles net before passing the puck out to Mantha at the top of the left circle. He stopped the puck with his skate, skated into the circle and avoided two defenders before snapping a shot past Forsberg. The Kings were outshot 14-3 in the second period after both teams combined for just nine shots in the first period. --Field Level Media

item.title: Inside the Trump-administration campaign to return Brazil’s Bolsonaro clan to power
item.description: Two US State Department officials pushed for sanctions aimed at tilting Brazil's election in their favor, according to multiple current and former US officials.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Stargardter
item.content:encoded: Two US State Department officials led a campaign to restore the right-wing Bolsonaro clan to power in Brazil and successfully pushed for sanctions aimed at tilting the election in their favor, according to 10 current and former US officials with direct knowledge of the matter. Their plan faces a reckoning on Sunday, when Senator Flavio Bolsonaro faces leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a tight run-off. Lula has warned Washington against encroaching on Brazil's sovereignty and accused his opponent of plotting with the Trump administration. The two officials were Darren Beattie, a Senior Advisor for Western Hemisphere Affairs who [USN:L1N3ZM12Y TEXT:"oversees Brazil policy"], and Ricardo Pita, another senior advisor promoted this year to Deputy Assistant Secretary for North America. The details of their campaign to return the Bolsonaros to power haven't been previously reported. Beattie and Pita, both political appointees, operated with wide latitude to manage Washington's relationship with the second most-populous country in the Americas, the people said. In the months before election campaigning began, they instructed US diplomats in Brazil that it was US policy to restore former President Jair Bolsonaro as Brazil’s leader – even though he had been disqualified from office for plotting a coup in 2022, when he lost the presidential election to Lula, three of the people said. After Bolsonaro received a [USN:S0N3UJ08N TEXT:"27-year sentence in September 2025"], the two men pivoted to supporting the candidacy of his son, right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the three sources said. Beattie and Pita told embassy staff not to interact with other conservative presidential contenders who could challenge the younger Bolsonaro, they said. Since last year, the two men have successfully advocated for punitive US government measures on Brazil designed to weaken Lula and boost the Bolsonaros, the 10 people told Reuters. The policies included designating Brazilian gangs as terrorist groups and imposing US sanctions against the Brazilian Supreme Court Justice who was spearheading the investigation into Jair Bolsonaro. Reuters could not determine the extent to which the two men were acting on orders from the White House or Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Trump, a vocal defender of Bolsonaro since his election defeat in 2022, hasn’t publicly endorsed any candidate. The White House declined to comment and referred questions to the State Department. State Department Spokesman Tommy Pigott didn't answer questions about specific measures and directives involving Beattie and Pita but said in a statement: "All actions taken by the United States against narco-traffickers and to protect free speech are to defend the rights and lives of the American people. The Brazilian people have the right to choose their leaders through free and fair elections." Lula’s office did not respond to comment requests. Orna Blum, one of the officials who spoke to Reuters about Beattie and Pita’s efforts, led the State Department's Brazil and Southern Cone office until retiring last year over her opposition to the Trump administration. Washington "has every right to pursue its economic and strategic interests," she said. "But when American foreign policy instruments are used to pressure another democracy over the legal fate of a political ally, the line between diplomacy and political intervention has been crossed." SANCTIONS ON A SUPREME COURT JUSTICE Beattie is a former White House speechwriter fired in 2018 after addressing an event frequented by white nationalists. He’s also the architect of " free speech diplomacy ," a policy advocated by Trump allies that seeks to punish nations they accuse of censoring right-wing speech by US citizens, companies and global right-wing allies. The United States has accused Brazil Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of violating free speech rights by jailing Brazilians for political social-media posts and by censoring content of US social-media companies. Moraes has argued he was ridding social media of fake news that undermined public faith in Brazil's democratic institutions. Moraes did not respond to a comment request. Pita, a conservative Venezuelan-American, is among many in Rubio's orbit who view Lula as a threat to US interests in Latin America. Rubio has been a key leader in the administration’s aggressive policy in the region, which has included an invasion of Venezuela to oust its president, an oil blockade of Cuba, and military attacks on suspected drug boats from Latin America. Beattie and Pita were drawn to the Bolsonaro family’s right-wing politics, their antipathy towards Lula, and the idea that Jair Bolsonaro was a victim of abuses by Brazil's Supreme Court. Like Trump in the 2020 US election, Bolsonaro refused to concede he lost Brazil’s 2022 presidential vote, triggering riots by supporters who stormed government buildings. The Supreme Court convicted him in September 2025 of plotting a coup to remain in power. Before the conviction, in early 2025, the Bolsonaros were aggressively lobbying Washington for sanctions under the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act against Moraes, who had led criminal investigations into Jair Bolsonaro. The act is a 2016 federal law allowing US sanctions against foreign individuals responsible for human-rights abuses or severe corruption. Around April 2025, Jair Bolsonaro’s younger son, Eduardo, visited Beattie in his State Department office in Washington DC, according to two former US officials.
